1.1: The Lord pulled up on Moses while they was out in the wilderness of Sinai, inside the meeting tent. This was the first day of the second month, two years after they bounced up outta Egypt. He said,
1.2: 'Go 'head and count up everybody in Israel. Do it by family, by their daddy's people, name by name, every dude one by one.
1.3: If they twenty or older and can fight, count 'em. You and Aaron gotta list 'em out by their squads.
1.4: And every tribe gotta send a man, the leader of his family, to help y'all with the count.
1.5: Here go the names of the ones rolling with you: from Reuben, Elizur, son of Shedeur;
1.6: From Simeon, Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai;
1.7: From Judah, Nahshon, son of Amminadab;
1.8: From Issachar, Nethanel, son of Zuar;
1.9: From Zebulun, Eliab, son of Helon;
1.10: From Joseph's people: from Ephraim, Elishama, son of Ammihud; from Manasseh, Gamaliel, son of Pedahzur;
1.11: From Benjamin, Abidan, son of Gideoni;
1.12: From Dan, Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai;
1.13: From Asher, Pagiel, son of Ocran;
1.14: From Gad, Eliasaph, son of Deuel;
1.15: From Naphtali, Ahira, son of Enan.
1.16: These the main dudes, the head honchos of their family tribes. The top dogs over all the squads of Israel.
1.17: Moses and Aaron took these men, the ones called out by name,
1.18: And on the first day of the second month, they got all the people together. They ran through everybody's family history, going by their daddy's side, and listed out everybody name by name, twenty and up.
1.19: Just like the Lord told Moses, he counted them up in the wilderness of Sinai.
1.20: From Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: all the men twenty and up, able to fight, counted by their family and daddy's house—
1.22: From Simeon, every dude twenty and up, ready for battle, counted by family—
1.24: From Gad, all the men twenty and up, ready to fight, counted by their family—
1.26: From Judah, every man twenty and up, war-ready, counted by family—
1.28: From Issachar, all the men twenty and up, ready to ride—
1.30: From Zebulun, every man twenty and up, suited up for war—
1.32: From Joseph's people, the Ephraim squad: every dude twenty and up, ready for battle—
1.34: From Manasseh, every man twenty and up, prepped for war—
1.36: From Benjamin, every dude twenty and up, down for the fight—
1.38: From Dan, all the men twenty and up, counted by family—
1.40: From Asher, all the men twenty and up, war-ready—
1.42: From Naphtali, every man twenty and up, suited up—
1.44: These the ones that got counted, the ones Moses and Aaron wrote down, plus the twelve leaders of Israel, one from each tribe.
1.45: So, after counting all the men twenty and up, ready to fight, by their family—
1.46: The grand total came up to 603,550.
1.47: But the Levites? They ain't get counted with the rest of 'em.
1.49: 'Don't count the tribe of Levi or put them in the mix with the rest of Israel.'
1.50: 'Instead, put them in charge of the tabernacle of the Testimony. They gon' handle all its stuff, move it when needed, and set it up when y'all stop. Ain't nobody else supposed to come near it.'
1.51: 'When it's time to move, the Levites gon' pack it up. When it's time to camp, they gon' set it up. If anybody else try to step up, they getting put down.'
1.52: 'Everybody else in Israel gotta camp by their own squad, under their family's banner.'
1.53: 'But the Levites? They gotta camp around the tabernacle, keeping it safe so my anger don't hit Israel. They gotta watch over the tabernacle like it's their main job.'
1.54: And that's exactly what Israel did. Just like the Lord told Moses, they followed through.

2.1: Then the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said,
2.2: 'Tell everybody in Israel they gotta set up camp under their family's banner, posted up by their squad's emblem. But they can't camp too close to the meeting tent.'
2.3: 'On the east side, where the sun comes up, Judah's crew gon' set up first, posted up by their squad. Nahshon, son of Amminadab, gon' be their leader.'
2.5: 'Next to them, Issachar's tribe gon' set up camp. Their leader is Nethanel, son of Zuar.'
2.7: 'Then Zebulun's tribe gon' set up next. Their leader is Eliab, son of Helon.'
2.9: 'All together, the whole squad rolling with Judah got 186,400 men. They gon' be the first to move when it's time to pack up.'
2.10: 'On the south side, Reuben's squad gon' camp together, set up by their banner. Their leader is Elizur, son of Shedeur.'
2.12: 'Next to them, Simeon's squad gon' set up. Their leader is Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai.'
2.14: 'Then Gad's tribe gon' set up camp. Their leader is Eliasaph, son of Reuel.'
2.16: 'All together, Reuben's squad got 151,450 men. They gon' be the second crew to roll out when it's time to move.'
2.17: 'Right in the middle of all the camps, the Levites gon' move with the meeting tent. Just like they camp in the middle, they gon' travel in the middle too, all in order, by their squads.'
2.18: 'On the west side, Ephraim's crew gon' camp under their banner. Their leader is Elishama, son of Ammihud.'
2.20: 'Next to them, Manasseh's tribe gon' set up camp. Their leader is Gamaliel, son of Pedahzur.'
2.22: 'Then Benjamin's tribe gon' set up. Their leader is Abidan, son of Gideoni.'
2.24: 'All together, Ephraim's crew got 108,100 men. They gon' be the third group to roll out when it's time to move.'
2.25: 'On the north side, Dan's squad gon' set up under their banner. Their leader is Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai.'
2.27: 'Next to them, Asher's squad gon' set up. Their leader is Pagiel, son of Ocran.'
2.29: 'Then Naphtali's tribe gon' set up. Their leader is Ahira, son of Enan.'
2.31: 'All together, Dan's squad got 157,600 men. They gon' be the last ones to move out, keeping it tight with their banner.'
2.32: 'That's everybody in Israel, counted up by their families. The total number of soldiers? 603,550 men.'
2.33: 'But the Levites? They wasn't included in the count, just like the Lord told Moses.'
2.34: So, Israel did exactly what the Lord commanded. They camped where they was supposed to be, under their banners, and when it was time to move, they rolled out in order, just like they was told.

3.1: Here go the records of Aaron and Moses from when the Lord spoke to Moses up on Mount Sinai.
3.2: These Aaron's sons: Nadab (his firstborn), Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
3.3: They was the ones anointed to be priests, set apart to do the Lord's work.
3.4: But Nadab and Abihu? They messed up bad—they tried to bring some disrespectful fire before the Lord out in the wilderness, and He took 'em out. Since they ain't have no kids, Eleazar and Ithamar stepped up and kept the priesthood going under Aaron's watch.
3.6: 'Bring the whole tribe of Levi to Aaron so they can help him out.'
3.7: 'They gon' take care of everything he need and look out for the whole congregation when it comes to the meeting tent. That's their job.'
3.8: 'They also gon' be in charge of the furniture in the meeting tent, plus all the work that gotta be done for Israel in that spot.'
3.9: 'The Levites belong to Aaron and his sons—fully dedicated to them from all the tribes of Israel.'
3.10: 'Aaron and his sons? They the only ones who can handle the priesthood. Anybody else tryna step up? They gettin' put down, no questions asked.'
3.12: 'Look, I'm claimin' the Levites instead of every firstborn son in Israel. They mine now.'
3.13: 'Every firstborn belongs to me—whether human or animal. The day I took out all the firstborn in Egypt, I set apart every firstborn in Israel for myself. They mine. I'm the Lord.'
3.14: Then the Lord told Moses while they was still out in the wilderness of Sinai,
3.15: 'Count up the Levites by their families, from their daddy's house. Every male one month old and up.'
3.16: So Moses did just that, just like the Lord told him.
3.17: Here go the main sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
3.19: Kohath's sons? Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
3.20: Merari's sons? Mahli and Mushi. That's the Levite families by their daddies.
3.21: Gershon's clan came from the Libnite and Shimite families. They was called the Gershonites.
3.22: All the Gershonite males one month old and up? 7,500 total.
3.23: The Gershonites set up camp west of the tabernacle.
3.24: Their leader was Eliasaph, son of Lael.
3.25: Their job was taking care of the tabernacle—the tent itself, the coverings, the entrance screen,
3.26: The courtyard curtains, the altar curtains, and all the ropes. Basically, anything related to those things.
3.27: Kohath's clan came from the Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites, and Uzzielites. They was called the Kohathites.
3.28: All the Kohathite males one month old and up? 8,600 total. They was in charge of guarding the holy place.
3.29: The Kohathites camped on the south side of the tabernacle.
3.30: Their leader was Elizaphan, son of Uzziel.
3.31: Their job was to handle the most sacred things—the Ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the sacred tools, the curtain, and everything that went with it.
3.32: Eleazar, Aaron's son, was over all the Levites, making sure everything in the holy place was taken care of.
3.33: Merari's clan came from the Mahlite and Mushite families. They was called the Merarites.
3.34: All the Merarite males one month old and up? 6,200 total.
3.35: Their leader was Zuriel, son of Abihail. They set up camp on the north side of the tabernacle.
3.36: Their job was to handle the structure of the tabernacle—the frames, crossbars, posts, bases,
3.37: And also the posts around the courtyard, their bases, tent pegs, and ropes. Anything structural, they was on it.
3.38: Moses, Aaron, and his sons set up camp right in front of the tabernacle on the east side, guarding the sacred place for all of Israel. But if anybody else tried to step up, they was gettin' put to death.
3.39: When Moses and Aaron finished counting all the Levite males one month old and up, it totaled 22,000.
3.40: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Count all the firstborn males in Israel, one month old and up. Write down their names.'
3.41: 'Then take the Levites as mine instead of the firstborn sons of Israel. Same goes for their livestock—the Levite animals replace Israel's firstborn animals. I'm the Lord.'
3.42: So Moses counted all the firstborn sons in Israel, just like the Lord told him.
3.43: The total number of firstborn males, one month old and up, was 22,273.
3.45: 'Take the Levites instead of Israel's firstborn sons, and their livestock instead of Israel's firstborn animals. The Levites belong to me. I'm the Lord.'
3.46: 'But there's 273 more firstborns than Levites, so here's what you gotta do.'
3.47: 'For each extra firstborn, collect five shekels in silver (the holy shekel, which is 20 gerahs).'
3.48: 'Take that money and hand it over to Aaron and his sons as their redemption fee.'
3.49: So Moses collected the silver from the extra firstborns beyond the number of Levites.
3.50: Total amount collected? 1,365 shekels, according to the holy shekel measurement.
3.51: Then Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons, just like the Lord told him.

4.1: Then the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
4.2: 'Count up all the sons of Kohath from the Levite tribe, by their families and their daddy's house.'
4.3: 'Everybody between 30 and 50 years old—the ones who gon' put in work at the meeting tent.'
4.4: 'This what the Kohath clan gotta do—they in charge of handling the holiest things inside the meeting tent.'
4.5: 'When it's time to move out, Aaron and his sons gotta go in first. They gotta take down the inner curtain and use it to cover the Ark of the Testimony.'
4.6: 'Then they wrap it with a layer of badger skin, lay a solid blue cloth on top, and slide in the carrying poles.'
4.7: 'They gon' spread a blue cloth over the table of showbread, then put all the dishes, pans, bowls, and pitchers on it—with the bread still in place.'
4.8: 'Then they cover it all with a red cloth, another layer of badger skin, and slide in the poles.'
4.9: 'They gon' wrap up the lampstand with a blue cloth, covering all the lamps, wick-trimmers, trays, and oil jars.'
4.10: 'After that, they wrap everything up in badger skins and put it on a carrying beam.'
4.11: 'For the golden altar, they lay a blue cloth over it, then a layer of badger skin, and slide in the poles.'
4.12: 'All the sacred tools used in the sanctuary? Wrap them in a blue cloth, cover them in badger skin, and put them on a carrying beam.'
4.13: 'They also gotta clean the ashes off the altar and cover it with a purple cloth.'
4.14: 'Then they put all the altar tools—firepans, forks, shovels, and basins—on top, cover it with badger skin, and slide in the poles.'
4.15: 'Once Aaron and his sons finish covering everything up and the camp is ready to move, the Kohathites come in and carry it all. But they can't touch none of it directly, or they gon' die.'
4.16: 'Eleazar, Aaron's son, got a special job—he's in charge of the oil for the lamp, the sweet incense, the daily grain offering, and the anointing oil. He oversees the whole sanctuary and all its furniture.'
4.17: Then the Lord told Moses and Aaron,
4.18: 'Don't let the Kohathite clan get wiped out from the Levites.'
4.19: 'Here's how you keep 'em safe when they handle the holy things: Aaron and his sons gotta assign each person their specific job.'
4.20: 'But they can't go in and watch when the sacred things are being covered, or they gon' die.'
4.22: 'Now count up the sons of Gershon, by their families and their daddy's house.'
4.23: 'Everybody between 30 and 50 years old, the ones who gon' work in the meeting tent, count 'em up.'
4.24: 'This their job when they serve and carry things:'
4.25: 'They handle the curtains of the tabernacle, the tent itself, its covering, the badger skin layer on top, and the screen for the entrance.'
4.26: 'They also take care of the courtyard screen, the hangings around the altar, all the cords, and everything that goes with these things.'
4.27: 'Aaron and his sons gon' assign all their work and give them their duties.'
4.28: 'That's what the Gershonites gotta do in the meeting tent, and their work is under Ithamar, Aaron's son.'
4.29: 'Now for the sons of Merari, count 'em by their families and daddy's house.'
4.30: 'Everybody between 30 and 50 years old, the ones working in the meeting tent, count 'em up.'
4.31: 'This what they carry for their work: the tabernacle's frame, crossbars, posts, and bases.'
4.32: 'Also, the courtyard posts, their bases, pegs, and ropes—plus everything they need to set it all up. Each man gotta be assigned what he's carrying by name.'
4.33: 'That's the job for the Merari clan. They work under Ithamar, Aaron's son.'
4.34: So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders counted the Kohathites by their families and their daddy's house.
4.35: Everybody between 30 and 50 years old, the ones working in the meeting tent, got counted.
4.36: The total number of Kohathites serving? 2,750.
4.37: These were the men officially counted from the Kohathite families, assigned to serve in the meeting tent, just like the Lord told Moses and Aaron.
4.38: The Gershonites were counted next, by their families and their daddy's house.
4.39: Everybody between 30 and 50 years old, working in the meeting tent, got counted.
4.40: The total number of Gershonites serving? 2,630.
4.41: That was the total from the Gershonite families, counted just like the Lord told Moses and Aaron.
4.42: Then came the count for the Merari clan, by their families and their daddy's house.
4.43: Everybody between 30 and 50 years old, working in the meeting tent, got counted.
4.44: The total number of Merarites serving? 3,200.
4.45: That was the total from the Merari families, counted just like the Lord told Moses and Aaron.
4.46: In total, all the Levites counted by Moses, Aaron, and the Israelite leaders, by their families and their daddy's houses—
4.47: Every man between 30 and 50 years old, assigned to work in the meeting tent and carry its loads—
4.49: They all got counted, just like the Lord told Moses, and got their assignments based on their specific duties. That's how Moses numbered them, just like God commanded.

5.1: Then the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
5.2: 'Tell the Israelites they gotta send out anybody with leprosy, anybody with a bodily discharge, or anybody who got made unclean from touching a dead body.'
5.3: 'Man or woman, don't matter—they gotta go outside the camp so they don't make the place unclean, 'cause I'm living right in the middle of y'all.'
5.4: And the Israelites did just that, sending them outside the camp, just like the Lord told Moses.
5.5: Then the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
5.6: 'Tell the people this: If a man or woman sins by doing wrong against the Lord, they guilty.'
5.7: 'They gotta confess their sin, pay back what they took or damaged, plus an extra 20%, and give it to the person they wronged.'
5.8: 'But if that person ain't got no relatives to receive the repayment, then it goes to the priest, along with a ram for atonement.'
5.9: 'Every offering the Israelites bring to the priest belongs to him.'
5.10: 'Whatever gift somebody brings to the priest, it's his to keep.'
5.11: Then the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
5.12: 'Tell the people: If a man's wife cheats on him and steps out,'
5.13: 'If she sleeps with another man and keeps it a secret—nobody sees it, and she don't get caught—'
5.14: 'But her husband starts feeling suspicious, whether she did it or not,'
5.15: 'He gotta take her to the priest, along with an offering of a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. No oil, no frankincense—it's a jealousy offering, meant to expose the truth.'
5.16: 'The priest gon' bring her forward and stand her before the Lord.'
5.17: 'Then he gon' take some holy water in a clay jar, mix in dust from the tabernacle floor, and stir it up.'
5.18: 'The priest gon' make the woman stand before the Lord, uncover her head, and put the jealousy offering in her hands. Meanwhile, he holding the bitter water that brings a curse.'
5.19: 'Then he gon' make her take an oath, saying, "If you ain't cheat, this bitter water won't do nothing to you."'
5.20: 'But if you did cheat on your husband and laid with another man—'
5.21: 'Then the priest gon' say, "May the Lord make you a curse among your people. May your belly swell and your thigh shrivel up."'
5.22:
'"May this cursed water go inside you, make your belly swell, and your thigh waste away."'
"Then the woman gotta say, 'Amen, so be it.'"
5.23: 'The priest then gon' write down the curse, wash the ink into the bitter water, and make her drink it.'
5.24: 'When she drinks it, if she guilty, it gon' do what it's supposed to do.'
5.25: 'The priest then gon' take the jealousy offering from her hands, wave it before the Lord, and put it on the altar.'
5.26: 'He gon' take a handful as a memorial portion, burn it on the altar, then make her drink the water.'
5.27: 'If she guilty, the water gon' make her stomach swell, her thigh rot, and she gon' be a curse among her people.'
5.28: 'But if she innocent and didn't cheat, she gon' be fine and able to have kids.'
5.29: 'This the law for handling jealousy—whether a woman really cheated or the husband just paranoid.'
5.30: 'Either way, the man gotta bring her before the Lord, and the priest gon' follow these steps.'
5.31: 'The man won't be guilty of anything, but if the woman did wrong, she gotta deal with the consequences.'

6.2: 'Tell the people of Israel this: If anybody—man or woman—wanna take a Nazirite vow and set themselves apart for the Lord,'
6.3: 'They gotta stay away from wine and any kind of liquor. No vinegar made from wine, no grape juice, and they can't even eat grapes or raisins.'
6.4: 'As long as they on this Nazirite vow, they can't have nothing that come from a grapevine—not even the seeds or the skin.'
6.5: 'They can't cut their hair the whole time they under this vow. They holy and set apart for the Lord, so they gotta let their hair grow out.'
6.6: 'They also can't go near a dead body the whole time they under this vow.'
6.7: 'Even if their own mama, daddy, brother, or sister die, they can't touch the body, 'cause their hair is a sign that they dedicated to God.'
6.8: 'This rule stays in place for the whole time they set apart for the Lord.'
6.9: 'If somebody drop dead next to them, their dedicated hair gets defiled. They gotta wait seven days, then shave their head to get clean again.'
6.10: 'On the eighth day, they gotta bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the meeting tent.'
6.11: 'The priest gon' sacrifice one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. That's how they get purified from the guilt of touching the dead body. Then, they gotta start over and let their hair grow again.'
6.12: 'Any days they completed before getting defiled don't count. They gotta rededicate themselves to the Lord and restart their full Nazirite time. Plus, they gotta bring a one-year-old male lamb for a guilt offering.'
6.13: 'When a Nazirite finishes their vow period, they gotta go to the entrance of the meeting tent.'
6.14: 'They gotta bring these offerings to the Lord: a one-year-old male lamb with no defects for a burnt offering, a one-year-old female lamb with no defects for a sin offering, and a ram with no defects for a peace offering.'
6.15: 'Also, a basket of bread with no yeast—cakes of fine flour mixed with olive oil and wafers spread with olive oil—plus the usual grain offerings and drink offerings.'
6.16: 'The priest gon' take all these offerings and present them to the Lord: first the sin offering and the burnt offering,'
6.17: 'Then the ram for the peace offering, along with the bread with no yeast. The priest also gon' offer the grain and drink offerings.'
6.18: 'Then the Nazirite gon' shave their head at the entrance of the meeting tent. They gotta take the hair they dedicated and burn it under the peace offering fire.'
6.19: 'After that, the priest gon' take the boiled shoulder of the ram, plus a cake and a wafer from the basket, and put it in the Nazirite's hands.'
6.20: 'Then the priest gon' lift these up as a special offering to the Lord. These holy portions go to the priest, just like the breast and thigh from the sacred offering. After this, the Nazirite can go back to drinking wine.'
6.21: 'That's the law for anybody taking a Nazirite vow and bringing these offerings to the Lord. If they got extra to give, they can bring more, but whatever they vowed to do, they gotta follow through completely.'
6.23: 'Tell Aaron and his sons to bless the people of Israel with this special blessing:'
6.24: 'May the Lord bless you and protect you.'
6.25: 'May the Lord smile on you and be gracious to you.'
6.26: 'May the Lord show you His favor and give you peace.'
6.27: 'Whenever Aaron and his sons bless the people in My name, I Myself will bless them.'

7.1: The day Moses set up the Tabernacle, he anointed it, made it holy, and set it apart for the Lord. He did the same for all the furniture, the altar, and all the tools that went with it.
7.2: Then the leaders of Israel—the heads of the tribes who had counted up all the soldiers—came forward with their offerings.
7.3: They brought six big wagons and twelve oxen. Every two leaders shared a wagon, and each leader brought one ox. They put all of this in front of the Tabernacle to offer it to the Lord.
7.5: 'Go ahead and take their gifts, and use these oxen and wagons to help move the Tabernacle. Divide them up among the Levites, based on their duties.'
7.6: So Moses took the wagons and oxen and gave them to the Levites.
7.7: The Gershonites got two wagons and four oxen for their work.
7.8: The Merarites got four wagons and eight oxen for their work. All of this was under Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.
7.9: But the Kohathites didn't get no wagons or oxen, 'cause their job was to carry the sacred items of the Tabernacle on their shoulders.
7.10: The leaders also brought dedication gifts for the altar the same day it was anointed. Each leader placed their offering in front of the altar.
7.11: The Lord told Moses, 'Each leader will bring their offering, one per day, for the dedication of the altar.'
7.12: On the first day, Nahshon son of Amminadab, leader of Judah, brought his offering.
7.13: He brought a silver plate weighing three and a quarter pounds and a silver bowl weighing one and three-quarters pounds (measured by the sanctuary shekel). Both were filled with grain offerings made from fine flour mixed with olive oil.
7.14: He also brought a gold container weighing four ounces, filled with incense.
7.15: For a burnt offering, he brought a young bull, a ram, and a one-year-old male lamb.
7.16: For a sin offering, he brought a male goat.
7.17: For a peace offering, he brought two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was Nahshon's offering.
7.18: On the second day, Nethanel son of Zuar, leader of Issachar, brought his offering.
7.19: He brought a silver plate weighing three and a quarter pounds and a silver bowl weighing one and three-quarters pounds (measured by the sanctuary shekel). Both were filled with grain offerings made from fine flour mixed with olive oil.
7.20: He also brought a gold container weighing four ounces, filled with incense.
7.21: For a burnt offering, he brought a young bull, a ram, and a one-year-old male lamb.

7.23: For a peace offering, he brought two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was Nethanel's offering.

7.33: For a burnt offering, he brought a young bull, a ram, and a one-year-old male lamb.

7.37: His offering was a silver plate weighing three and a quarter pounds and a silver bowl weighing one and three-quarters pounds (measured by the sanctuary shekel). Both were filled with grain offerings made from fine flour mixed with olive oil.
7.38: He also brought a gold container weighing four ounces, filled with incense.
7.39: For a burnt offering, he brought a young bull, a ram, and a one-year-old male lamb.

7.43: His offering was a silver plate weighing three and a quarter pounds and a silver bowl weighing one and three-quarters pounds (measured by the sanctuary shekel). Both were filled with grain offerings made from fine flour mixed with olive oil.

8.2: 'Tell Aaron this: When you set up the seven lamps on the lampstand, make sure they shine forward, lighting up everything in front of it.'
8.3: So Aaron did exactly that—he set up the seven lamps so they shined forward, just like the Lord told Moses.
8.4: The whole lampstand, from the base to the fancy designs on it, was made out of pure hammered gold. It was built exactly like the design the Lord showed Moses.
8.6: 'Set the Levites apart from the rest of the Israelites and make them ceremonially clean.'
8.7: 'Here's how you do it: Sprinkle them with the special purification water, have them shave off all their hair, and wash their clothes. That's how they get clean.'
8.8: 'Then they gotta bring a young bull with a grain offering of fine flour mixed with olive oil, plus another young bull for a sin offering.'
8.9: 'Gather all the Israelites at the entrance of the meeting tent and bring the Levites forward.'
8.10: 'When you present the Levites before the Lord, the Israelites gotta lay their hands on them as a sign of dedication.'
8.11: 'Then Aaron gon' raise his hands and present the Levites to the Lord as a special offering from the people, dedicating them to serve Him.'
8.12: 'After that, the Levites gotta lay their hands on the heads of the young bulls. One bull is for a sin offering, the other for a burnt offering to make them right with the Lord.'
8.13: 'Then line up the Levites in front of Aaron and his sons, and lift them up as a special offering to the Lord.'
8.14: 'This is how you officially set the Levites apart—they belong to Me now, not the rest of Israel.'
8.15: 'Once that's done, they can start working in the meeting tent, 'cause they been purified and dedicated as a special offering.'
8.16: 'Out of all the Israelites, the Levites are My chosen ones. I took them instead of the firstborn sons of Israel.'
8.17: 'Every firstborn—human or animal—already belongs to Me. I set them apart for Myself on the day I took out all the firstborn in Egypt.'
8.18: 'Now, instead of taking every firstborn from Israel, I'm taking the Levites as their replacement.'
8.19: 'I'm giving the Levites to Aaron and his sons to help run the meeting tent, offering sacrifices on behalf of the Israelites, and making sure no plagues hit them when they approach My sanctuary.'
8.20: So Moses, Aaron, and all the Israelites did exactly what the Lord commanded about dedicating the Levites.
8.21: The Levites cleaned themselves, washed their clothes, and Aaron lifted them up, presenting them as a special offering to the Lord. Then he made a sacrifice to purify them and make them right with the Lord.
8.22: After that, the Levites went into the meeting tent and started doing their duties, helping Aaron and his sons. They followed everything the Lord told Moses to do concerning them.
8.24: 'Here's the rule for the Levites: They start working in the meeting tent at 25 years old.'
8.25: 'But when they hit 50, they gotta retire from their regular service.'
8.26: 'After that, they can still assist their fellow Levites by guarding the meeting tent, but they can't do the main work anymore. This is how you handle their assignments.'

9.1: A year after Israel left Egypt, the Lord spoke to Moses while they was out in the wilderness of Sinai. This was during the first month of that year.
9.2: The Lord said, 'Tell the Israelites they gotta celebrate Passover at the set time.'
9.3: 'They gotta do it at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month. Make sure they follow all my rules and instructions for this celebration.'
9.4: So Moses told the people to celebrate the Passover.
9.5: They kept the festival out in the wilderness of Sinai at twilight on the fourteenth day of the month, just like the Lord told Moses.
9.6: But some men had touched a dead body and became ceremonially unclean, so they couldn't celebrate Passover that day. They came to Moses and Aaron.
9.7: They said, 'We unclean 'cause we touched a dead body. But why should that stop us from presenting the Lord's offering at the right time like everybody else?'
9.8: Moses told them, 'Hold up. Let me go ask the Lord and see what He says about this.'
9.9: Then the Lord gave Moses His answer.
9.10: 'Tell the Israelites this: If somebody gets unclean 'cause they touched a dead body during Passover time, or if they on a trip and can't be there, they still get a chance to celebrate.'
9.11: 'They gotta do the Passover sacrifice one month later, at twilight on the fourteenth day of the second month. They gotta eat the lamb with bitter herbs and unleavened bread.'
9.12: 'They can't leave none of the lamb till the next morning, and they can't break none of its bones. They still gotta follow all the usual Passover rules.'
9.13: 'But if somebody clean and ain't traveling, yet still don't celebrate Passover, they getting cut off from Israel. They ain't bringing their offering to the Lord at the right time, so they gotta deal with the guilt.'
9.14: 'If a foreigner living among y'all wanna celebrate Passover to honor the Lord, they gotta follow the same rules and laws as native Israelites. The same law applies to both.'
9.15: The day they set up the Tabernacle, a cloud covered it. But from evening to morning, that cloud over the Tabernacle looked like fire.
9.16: This kept happening every night—the cloud that covered the Tabernacle had the appearance of fire.
9.17: Whenever the cloud lifted from over the sacred tent, the Israelites would pack up and move. And wherever the cloud stopped, that's where they set up camp.
9.18: They traveled and camped only when the Lord told them to. When the cloud stayed put, they stayed put.
9.19: If the cloud stayed over the Tabernacle for a long time, the Israelites stayed in camp and followed what the Lord told them to do.
9.20: Sometimes the cloud would only stay for a few days. When that happened, they camped for a few days, just like the Lord commanded. Then when the Lord said move, they packed up and moved.
9.21: Sometimes the cloud only stayed overnight and lifted the next morning. But whether it was day or night, as soon as the cloud lifted, the Israelites packed up and moved out.
9.22: It didn't matter if the cloud stayed for two days, a month, or even a whole year. If it stayed, the people stayed. But when it lifted, they packed up and moved out.
9.23: So whether they camped or traveled, they did it at the Lord's command. They followed whatever the Lord told them to do through Moses.

10.2: 'Make two trumpets out of hammered silver. Use 'em to call everybody together and to signal when it's time to pack up and move.'
10.3: 'When both trumpets get blown, everybody gotta gather at the entrance of the Tabernacle.'
10.4: 'But if only one trumpet blows, then just the leaders—the heads of Israel's clans—need to come meet with you.'
10.5: 'When it's time to move, blow the first signal, and the tribes camped on the east side of the Tabernacle gotta break camp and head out.'
10.6: 'When you blow the second signal, the tribes camped on the south side gotta move next. Each move-out signal gotta be short blasts.'
10.7: 'But if you just calling everybody together for a meeting, blow a different sound on the trumpets.'
10.8: 'Only the priests—Aaron's sons—can blow these trumpets. This rule gon' last forever, passed down from generation to generation.'
10.9: 'When y'all get to the land I'm giving you and enemies come to attack, blow the alarm on the trumpets. Then the Lord your God gon' remember y'all and rescue y'all from your enemies.'
10.10: 'Blow them trumpets when y'all celebrating too—at your festivals and at the start of every month. Blow them over your burnt offerings and peace offerings. That sound gon' remind your God of His covenant with y'all. I am the Lord your God.'
10.11: In the second year after Israel left Egypt—on the twentieth day of the second month—the cloud lifted up from the Tabernacle of the Covenant.
10.12: So the Israelites packed up and left the wilderness of Sinai, traveling from place to place until the cloud stopped in the wilderness of Paran.
10.13: That was the first time they set out, following the instructions the Lord gave Moses.
10.14: Judah's army led the way, marching behind their banner. Their leader was Nahshon son of Amminadab.
10.15: Right behind them was Issachar's army, led by Nethanel son of Zuar.
10.16: Next was Zebulun's army, led by Eliab son of Helon.
10.17: Then the Tabernacle got taken down, and the Gershonite and Merarite Levites set out next, carrying it with them.
10.18: Then came Reuben's army, marching behind their banner. Their leader was Elizur son of Shedeur.
10.19: Following them was Simeon's army, led by Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
10.20: Then came Gad's army, led by Eliasaph son of Deuel.
10.21: Next came the Kohathite Levites, carrying the sacred objects from the Tabernacle. By the time they got to the next campsite, the Tabernacle would already be set up.
10.22: Then came Ephraim's army, marching behind their banner. Their leader was Elishama son of Ammihud.
10.23: Right behind them was Manasseh's army, led by Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
10.24: Then came Benjamin's army, led by Abidan son of Gideoni.
10.25: Dan's army was last, marching behind their banner as the rear guard for all the tribes. Their leader was Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
10.26: Following them was Asher's army, led by Pagiel son of Ocran.
10.27: And then Naphtali's army, led by Ahira son of Enan.
10.28: This was the order in which the Israelites marched, tribe by tribe, division by division.
10.29: One day Moses told his brother-in-law, Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, 'We heading to the land the Lord promised us. He said He gon' give it to us. Come with us, and we'll treat you right, 'cause the Lord promised good things for Israel!'
10.30: But Hobab said, 'Nah, I ain't coming. I'm going back home to my land and my family.'
10.31: Moses pleaded, 'Please don't go. You know this wilderness better than we do. You can help guide us where to set up camp.'
10.32: 'If you come with us, you gon' get a share of all the blessings the Lord gives us.'
10.33: After they left the mountain of the Lord, they marched for three days, with the Ark of the Lord's Covenant going ahead of them to show 'em where to stop and rest.
10.34: As they traveled, the cloud of the Lord stayed above them, covering them.
10.35: Whenever the Ark set out, Moses would shout, 'Rise up, Lord! Scatter your enemies! Let all who hate you run away!'
10.36: And when the Ark stopped, he would say, 'Come back, Lord, and stay with the countless thousands of Israel!'

11.1: Not long after, the people started complaining about how hard things were, and the Lord heard everything they said. He got real mad and sent fire through the camp, burning up some folks on the outskirts.
11.2: Then the people started yelling for Moses to help. He prayed to the Lord, and the fire stopped.
11.3: After that, they called that place Taberah (meaning 'the place of burning') 'cause the Lord's fire had burned through there.
11.4: The outsiders traveling with Israel started craving the good food they had in Egypt. Soon, the Israelites joined in, complaining, 'Man, we need some meat!'
11.5: 'Remember all that fish we used to eat for free in Egypt? Plus the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic?'
11.6: 'Now we ain't got no appetite left. All we got is this manna, over and over again!'
11.7: The manna looked like small coriander seeds, and it had a pale yellow color, kinda like gum resin.
11.8: The people went out, picked it up, ground it into flour with hand mills or mortars, then boiled it and made flat cakes. It tasted like pastries baked with olive oil.
11.9: The manna came down at night along with the dew and covered the camp.
11.10: Moses heard families standing outside their tents whining, and the Lord got furious. Moses was fed up too.
11.11: Moses said to the Lord, 'Why you doing this to me, Lord? I been serving you, but why you putting all these people's problems on me?'
11.12: 'Did I birth these people? Did I bring them into the world? Why you telling me to carry them like a mama carries a baby? How am I supposed to get them to the land you promised their ancestors?'
11.13: 'Where am I supposed to find meat for all these folks? They keep whining to me, "Give us some meat to eat!"'
11.14: 'I can't do this by myself! It's too much!'
11.15: 'Lord, if this how it's gonna be, just go 'head and take me out now. Don't let me go out like this!'
11.16: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Gather seventy respected elders of Israel, the ones everybody knows as leaders. Bring them to the Tabernacle to stand with you.'
11.17: 'I'm coming down to talk with you there. I'ma take some of the Spirit that's on you and put it on them too. They gon' help you carry the burden of leading these people so you ain't gotta do it alone.'
11.18: 'Now go tell the people: Get yourselves right, 'cause tomorrow y'all getting meat. Y'all was crying, saying, "Oh, we had it so good in Egypt. We need some meat!" Now the Lord gon' give y'all what you want.'
11.19: 'And it ain't gon' be for just one day, or two, or five, or ten, or even twenty.'
11.20: 'Nah, y'all gon' eat meat for a whole month—till you can't stand it no more, till you gag on it. Y'all disrespected the Lord, the One right here with you, crying, "Why did we even leave Egypt?"'
11.21: Moses said, 'Lord, there's 600,000 soldiers with me, and you saying you gon' give them meat for a whole month?'
11.22: 'Even if we killed every animal we got, would that be enough? Even if we caught all the fish in the sea, would that be enough?'
11.23: The Lord said, 'Moses, you think my power too weak? Just watch—you 'bout to see if what I said gon' happen or not!'
11.24: So Moses went and told the people what the Lord said. Then he gathered seventy elders and had them stand around the Tabernacle.
11.25: The Lord came down in a cloud and spoke to Moses. Then He took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and put it on the seventy elders. When the Spirit hit them, they started prophesying—but that was a one-time thing.
11.26: Two men, Eldad and Medad, stayed in the camp. They were on the list of elders but didn't go to the Tabernacle. Even still, the Spirit came on them, and they started prophesying in the camp.
11.27: A young man ran to Moses and said, 'Eldad and Medad over there prophesying in the camp!'
11.28: Joshua, son of Nun, Moses' right-hand man since he was young, said, 'Moses, my master, tell them to stop!'
11.29: But Moses said, 'You jealous for me? I wish all the Lord's people had His Spirit on them and could prophesy!'
11.30: Then Moses and the elders went back to the camp.
11.31: The Lord sent a strong wind that blew in quail from the sea. They fell all around the camp, flying about three feet above the ground for miles in every direction.
11.32: The people went out and caught quail all day, all night, and all the next day. Nobody gathered less than fifty bushels! They spread the meat all over the camp to dry it out.
11.33: But while they was still stuffing their faces, before they even finished chewing, the Lord's anger flared up. He sent a severe plague, and people started dropping dead.
11.34: That place got named Kibroth-hattaavah (which means 'graves of gluttony'), 'cause that's where they buried the folks who got greedy for meat.
11.35: From Kibroth-hattaavah, the Israelites traveled to Hazeroth and stayed there for a while.

12.1: While they was at Hazeroth, Miriam and Aaron started talking bad about Moses 'cause he had married a Cushite woman.
12.2: They said, 'Ain't the Lord spoken through us too? Moses ain't the only one He talks to!' But the Lord heard them.
12.3: (Now Moses was real humble—more humble than anybody else on earth.)
12.4: So right away, the Lord called out to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam and said, 'All three of y'all, get to the Tabernacle!' So they all went.
12.5: Then the Lord came down in the pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the Tabernacle. He called out, 'Aaron! Miriam!' And they stepped forward.
12.6: Then the Lord said, 'Now listen to what I gotta say:'
12.7: 'If there were prophets among y'all, I would reveal myself in visions. I would speak to them in dreams.'
12.8: 'But not with my servant Moses. Out of everybody, he's the one I trust.'
12.9: 'I talk to him face to face, clear as day—not in riddles! He sees the Lord exactly as I am.'
12.10: 'So why did y'all feel bold enough to come at my servant Moses like that?'
12.11: The Lord got real mad at them and left.
12.12: As soon as the cloud lifted from the Tabernacle, Miriam was standing there—her skin white as snow from leprosy. When Aaron saw her, he was shook.
12.13: Aaron turned to Moses and said, 'Oh, my master! Please don't let us be punished for this sin we so foolishly committed.'
12.14: 'Don't let her be like a stillborn baby, halfway decayed as soon as it's born!'
12.15: So Moses cried out to the Lord, 'O God, please! Heal her now!'
12.16: But the Lord said to Moses, 'If her daddy had spit in her face, wouldn't she be shamed for seven days? Let her stay outside the camp for seven days, then she can come back.'
12.17: So Miriam was put outside the camp for seven days, and the people didn't move until she was allowed back in.
12.18: Then they left Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.

13.1: Then the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
13.2: 'Send some men to check out the land of Canaan—the land I'm giving to the Israelites. Pick one leader from each tribe.'
13.3: So Moses sent them out from the wilderness of Paran, just like the Lord told him to. All of them were top leaders of Israel.
13.4: Here go their names: From Reuben's tribe—Shammua, son of Zaccur.
13.5: From Simeon's tribe—Shaphat, son of Hori.
13.6: From Judah's tribe—Caleb, son of Jephunneh.
13.7: From Issachar's tribe—Igal, son of Joseph.
13.8: From Ephraim's tribe—Hoshea (Joshua), son of Nun.
13.9: From Benjamin's tribe—Palti, son of Raphu.
13.10: From Zebulun's tribe—Gaddiel, son of Sodi.
13.11: From Joseph's tribe, specifically Manasseh—Gaddi, son of Susi.
13.12: From Dan's tribe—Ammiel, son of Gemalli.
13.13: From Asher's tribe—Sethur, son of Michael.
13.14: From Naphtali's tribe—Nahbi, son of Vophsi.
13.15: From Gad's tribe—Geuel, son of Machi.
13.16: These are the names of the men Moses sent to spy on Canaan. Moses gave Hoshea, son of Nun, the name Joshua.
13.17: Moses sent them to spy on the land of Canaan and told them, 'Go through the southern region, then up into the mountains.'
13.18: 'Check out the land—see if the people living there strong or weak, if there's a lot of them or just a few.'
13.19: 'See if the land is good or bad, and if the cities got strong walls or if they just out in the open.'
13.20: 'Check if the land is rich or poor, and if it got forests or not. Be brave. And bring back some fruit from the land.' (It was grape harvest season.)
13.21: So they went up and spied on the land, from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob, near the entrance of Hamath.
13.22: They went through the southern part and reached Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai—the descendants of Anak—were. (Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.)
13.23: Then they got to the Valley of Eshcol, cut down a big cluster of grapes, and had to carry it on a pole between two of them. They also grabbed some pomegranates and figs.
13.24: They named the place Valley of Eshcol ('cause of the cluster of grapes they found there).
13.25: After forty days of spying, they came back.
13.26: They returned to Moses, Aaron, and the whole Israelite community in the wilderness of Paran at Kadesh. They reported back and showed off the fruit they brought.
13.27: They said, 'We went to the land you sent us to. And yeah, it really does flow with milk and honey! Check out this fruit!'
13.28: 'But the people there strong, and the cities got high walls—real big. We even saw Anak's descendants there!'
13.29: 'The Amalekites live in the south, the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the mountains, and the Canaanites live by the sea and the Jordan River.'
13.30: Then Caleb spoke up, tryna calm everybody down. He said, 'Nah, let's go take the land now. We got this!'
13.31: But the other spies with him said, 'Nah, we can't go against them. They stronger than us.'
13.32: They spread a bad report among the Israelites, saying, 'That land eats up the people living in it! And everybody we saw there was huge!'
13.33: 'We even saw giants—the descendants of Anak. Compared to them, we felt like grasshoppers. And they probably thought the same thing about us!'

14.1: The whole community started crying loud, and they wept all night.
14.2: Everybody started protesting against Moses and Aaron, saying, 'Man, we should've just died in Egypt—or even out here in this wilderness!'
14.3: 'Why the Lord bringing us to this land just for us to die in battle? Our wives and kids gon' get taken as slaves! Ain't it better for us to just go back to Egypt?'
14.4: Then they started plotting, saying, 'We should pick a new leader and head back to Egypt!'
14.5: When Moses and Aaron heard this, they fell face down on the ground in front of the whole community.
14.6: Joshua (son of Nun) and Caleb (son of Jephunneh), who were among the men who explored the land, tore their clothes in distress.
14.7: They told the whole Israelite community, 'The land we checked out is amazing—it's a good land!'
14.8: 'If the Lord happy with us, He gon' bring us into this land and give it to us. It's flowing with milk and honey!'
14.9: 'But y'all better not turn on the Lord. Don't be scared of them people in the land. They ain't nothing but prey to us! They got no protection, but the Lord is with us! Don't be scared of them!'
14.10: But the people started talking about stoning Joshua and Caleb. Then the glory of the Lord appeared to all the Israelites at the Tabernacle.
14.11: The Lord said to Moses, 'How long these people gon' keep disrespecting me? How long they gon' refuse to believe me, even after all the miracles I done for them?'
14.12: 'I'ma wipe them out with a plague and disown them. Then I'ma make a new nation outta you—one stronger and greater than them.'
14.13: But Moses said, 'Lord, what the Egyptians gon' say when they hear about this?'
14.14: 'They know all about your power and how you brought these people out of Egypt.'
14.15: 'If you wipe 'em out now, the nations who heard about you gon' be talking.'
14.16: 'They gon' say, "The Lord wasn't strong enough to bring them into the land He promised, so He killed them in the wilderness."'
14.17: 'Please, Lord, show your power just like you said you would.'
14.18: 'You said: "The Lord is slow to anger, full of love, forgiving sin and rebellion. But He don't let the guilty go free. The sins of the parents affect the kids, even up to the third and fourth generation."'
14.19: 'So in your great mercy, forgive these people, just like you been forgiving them since they left Egypt.'
14.20: Then the Lord said, 'Alright, I'ma pardon them like you asked.'
14.21: 'But as surely as I live, and as surely as my glory fills the whole earth—'
14.22: 'None of these people who saw my miracles in Egypt and in the wilderness, and still kept testing me, refusing to obey—'
14.23: 'None of them gon' see the land I promised their ancestors. Anybody who disrespected me ain't getting in.'
14.24: 'But my servant Caleb? He got a different spirit—he stayed loyal to me. So I'ma bring him into the land he explored, and his descendants gon' inherit it.'
14.25: 'Now turn back. Don't go toward the land of the Amalekites and Canaanites. Tomorrow, y'all gotta head toward the wilderness, back toward the Red Sea.'
14.26: Then the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron.
14.27: 'How long I gotta put up with these wicked people and all their complaining about me?'
14.28: 'Tell them this: As surely as I live, I'ma do exactly what y'all been saying.'
14.29: 'Y'all said you was gon' die in the wilderness? Well, everybody 20 and older who was counted in the census—y'all gon' drop dead out here.'
14.30: 'Ain't none of y'all gon' see the land I promised—except Caleb (son of Jephunneh) and Joshua (son of Nun).'
14.31: 'Y'all said your kids would be taken as slaves? Nah, they gon' enter the land y'all rejected, and they gon' enjoy it.'
14.32: 'But y'all? Y'all gon' die out here in this wilderness.'
14.33: 'Your kids gon' wander for 40 years, dealing with the consequences of y'all's disobedience, until the last one of y'all is gone.'
14.34: 'Since y'all spied on the land for 40 days, y'all gon' wander for 40 years—one year for every day, feeling what it's like to be against me.'
14.35: 'I, the Lord, have spoken! I'ma do this to every single person in this wicked community who turned against me. They gon' die out here in the wilderness.'
14.36: The ten men Moses sent to explore the land—the ones who spread the bad report and caused rebellion—
14.37: The Lord struck them down with a plague, and they died right then and there.
14.38: Of all the twelve spies, only Joshua (son of Nun) and Caleb (son of Jephunneh) survived.
14.39: When Moses told all this to the Israelites, they were filled with grief.
14.40: Early the next morning, they went to the top of the hills and said, 'Alright, let's go! We know we messed up, but now we ready to enter the land the Lord promised us!'
14.41: But Moses said, 'Why y'all tryna go now? The Lord already told y'all to turn back. This ain't gon' work.'
14.42: 'Don't go up there. Y'all gon' get beat bad, 'cause the Lord ain't with y'all.'
14.43: 'If y'all try to fight the Amalekites and Canaanites, they gon' destroy y'all. Since y'all turned away from the Lord, He ain't fighting for y'all no more.'
14.44: But they ignored Moses and pushed forward into the hill country. Neither Moses nor the Ark of the Lord's Covenant left the camp.
14.45: Then the Amalekites and Canaanites came down from the hills, attacked them, and chased them all the way back to Hormah.

15.2: 'Tell the Israelites this: When y'all finally settle in the land I'm giving you—'
15.3: 'Y'all gotta bring special gifts as an offering to the Lord, a sweet smell that pleases Him. These offerings can be burnt sacrifices, vows, voluntary offerings, or festival offerings, and they can come from your cattle, sheep, or goats.'
15.4: 'Whenever y'all bring an offering, you also gotta bring a grain offering—two quarts of fine flour mixed with a quart of olive oil.'
15.5: 'For each lamb y'all sacrifice, also bring a quart of wine as a drink offering to the Lord.'
15.6: 'If you sacrificing a ram, bring four quarts of fine flour mixed with a third of a gallon of olive oil.'
15.7: 'Also, bring a third of a gallon of wine as a drink offering. That's how y'all make a pleasing aroma to the Lord.'
15.8: 'If y'all bringing a young bull as a burnt offering, a vow offering, or a peace offering to the Lord—'
15.9: 'You gotta add a grain offering—six quarts of fine flour mixed with two quarts of olive oil.'
15.10: 'And also bring two quarts of wine as a drink offering. That's a special gift, a pleasing smell to the Lord.'
15.11: 'Do this same thing for every bull, ram, lamb, or young goat y'all sacrifice.'
15.12: 'Y'all gotta follow these instructions for every offering you bring.'
15.13: 'All native-born Israelites gotta follow these rules whenever they bring a special gift to the Lord.'
15.14: 'And if any foreigners visit or live among y'all and they wanna bring an offering to the Lord, they gotta follow the same rules.'
15.15: 'Everybody—both Israelites and foreigners—gotta follow the same laws before the Lord. This rule gon' last forever.'
15.16: 'The same instructions and laws apply to everybody, whether you was born in Israel or not.'
15.18: 'Tell the Israelites this: When y'all enter the land I'm bringing y'all to—'
15.19: 'And when y'all start eating from the crops grown there, set some aside as an offering to the Lord.'
15.20: 'Make a cake from the first of your ground flour and offer it up, just like y'all do with grain from the threshing floor.'
15.21: 'From now on, y'all gotta offer the first part of your flour to the Lord every year.'
15.22: 'But if y'all accidentally fail to follow all these commands I gave through Moses—'
15.23: 'Or if your descendants later on forget to obey what I commanded—'
15.24: 'If the mistake was made by the whole community without realizing it, then y'all gotta offer a young bull as a burnt offering. It must have no defects. This gotta be a pleasing aroma to the Lord.'
15.25: 'The priest will make atonement for the whole community, and they will be forgiven since it was unintentional. The burnt offering and the sin offering will cover them.'
15.26: 'The whole Israelite community will be forgiven, including any foreigners living with y'all, since everybody was involved in the sin.'
15.27: 'If one person sins unintentionally, they gotta bring a one-year-old female goat as a sin offering.'
15.28: 'The priest will sacrifice it to purify them before the Lord, and they will be forgiven.'
15.29: 'The same rule applies to both native Israelites and foreigners living among y'all.'
15.30: 'But if somebody deliberately disrespects the Lord's commands, whether they an Israelite or a foreigner, they gotta be cut off from the community.'
15.31: 'Since they treated the Lord's word with disrespect and refused to obey, they must be completely cut off and face the consequences.'
15.32: One day, while the Israelites were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath.
15.33: The people who caught him took him to Moses, Aaron, and the whole community.
15.34: They put him in custody 'cause they ain't know what to do with him yet.
15.35: Then the Lord said to Moses, 'The man must be put to death. The whole community must stone him outside the camp.'
15.36: So the whole community took him outside the camp and stoned him to death, just like the Lord commanded Moses.
15.38: 'Tell the Israelites this: From now on, throughout all generations, y'all gotta put tassels on the edges of your clothes and attach them with a blue cord.'
15.39: 'Whenever you see these tassels, they will remind you to obey all my commands instead of chasing after your own desires and falling into sin.'
15.40: 'They will help y'all remember that you must obey all my commands and stay holy before your God.'
15.41: 'I am the Lord your God. I brought y'all outta Egypt so I could be your God. I am the Lord your God!'

16.1: One day, Korah (son of Izhar, from Kohath's family in the tribe of Levi) teamed up with Dathan and Abiram (sons of Eliab) and On (son of Peleth) from the tribe of Reuben.
16.2: They convinced 250 other leaders—respected men in the community—to join them in a rebellion against Moses.
16.3: They came together against Moses and Aaron, saying, 'Y'all doing too much! The whole community is set apart by the Lord, and He's with all of us. What makes y'all think y'all better than the rest of us?'
16.4: When Moses heard this, he dropped face down to the ground.
16.5: Then he told Korah and his people, 'Tomorrow morning, the Lord gon' show everybody who really belongs to Him and who is holy. He gon' let the ones He chooses come near Him.'
16.6: 'Korah, you and all your followers, go prepare your incense burners.'
16.7: 'Tomorrow, y'all light the incense and burn it before the Lord. Then we'll see who the Lord picks as holy. Y'all Levites the ones doing too much!'
16.8: Then Moses spoke directly to Korah: 'Listen up, you Levites!'
16.9: 'Ain't it enough that the God of Israel picked y'all from the rest of the Israelites so y'all could serve Him in the Tabernacle and minister to the people?'
16.10: 'Korah, He already gave you and the other Levites this special role, and now y'all out here demanding the priesthood too?'
16.11: 'You and your crew ain't just coming at Aaron—you really rebelling against the Lord!'
16.12: Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, but they said, 'Nah, we ain't coming!'
16.13: 'Ain't it bad enough you took us from Egypt—a land flowing with milk and honey—just to leave us out here in the wilderness to die? Now you tryna rule over us too?'
16.14: 'You ain't brought us into no promised land with fields and vineyards! You think you can fool these people? We ain't coming!'
16.15: Moses got real mad and said to the Lord, 'Don't accept their offerings! I ain't took nothing from them—not even a donkey—and I ain't done them no wrong!'
16.16: Then Moses told Korah, 'You and all your people, come before the Lord tomorrow—Aaron gon' be there too.'
16.17: 'Each one of y'all, bring your incense burner with incense in it, and let's see what happens before the Lord.'
16.18: So they all brought their incense burners, lit the fire, and stood at the entrance of the Tabernacle with Moses and Aaron.
16.19: Meanwhile, Korah got the whole community riled up against Moses and Aaron. They all gathered at the Tabernacle entrance. Then the Lord's presence showed up.
16.20: The Lord told Moses and Aaron,
16.21: 'Step away from these people. I'ma wipe them out right now!'
16.22: But Moses and Aaron dropped face down and said, 'O God, you the one who gives life to all things. Will you destroy everybody just 'cause of one man's sin?'
16.24: 'Tell everybody to step away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.'
16.25: So Moses got up, went to Dathan and Abiram's tents, and the elders followed him.
16.26: He told the people, 'Move away from these wicked men's tents! Don't touch nothing that belongs to them, or you gon' be caught up in their punishment.'
16.27: So the people backed away from Korah, Dathan, and Abiram's tents. Then Dathan and Abiram came out, standing at their tent entrances with their wives and kids.
16.28: Moses said, 'This how y'all gon' know that the Lord sent me to do all this—not just me acting on my own.'
16.29: 'If these men die naturally, then the Lord ain't really sent me.'
16.30: 'But if something brand new happens—like the ground opening up and swallowing them alive—then y'all know these men have disrespected the Lord.'
16.31: As soon as Moses finished speaking, the ground suddenly split open under them.
16.32: The earth opened up and swallowed them, along with their families, followers, and all their belongings.
16.33: They went down alive into the grave with everything they had. Then the earth closed up over them, and they were gone from the Israelite community.
16.34: Everybody around them ran, screaming, 'The earth gon' swallow us too!'
16.35: Then fire shot out from the Lord and burned up the 250 men who had offered incense.
16.37: 'Tell Eleazar (Aaron's son, the priest) to collect all the incense burners from the ashes, 'cause they holy. Also, scatter the burning coals.'
16.38: 'The incense burners belong to the men who died. Take the bronze and hammer it into a thin sheet to cover the altar. These burners were used in the Lord's presence, so now they holy. Let them be a reminder to Israel.'
16.39: So Eleazar took the 250 bronze incense burners and had them hammered into a covering for the altar.
16.40: That way, no unauthorized person—nobody outside of Aaron's descendants—would ever try to burn incense before the Lord again. If they did, they'd end up like Korah and his crew. So Moses followed what the Lord commanded.
16.41: But the very next morning, the whole community started complaining against Moses and Aaron again, saying, 'Y'all killed the Lord's people!'
16.42: As they gathered against Moses and Aaron, they turned toward the Tabernacle and saw that the cloud had covered it, and the Lord's presence appeared.
16.43: Moses and Aaron stepped up to the front of the Tabernacle.
16.45: 'Move away from these people. I'ma wipe them out immediately!' But Moses and Aaron fell face down.
16.46: Moses told Aaron, 'Hurry! Grab an incense burner, put burning coals from the altar in it, add incense, and take it out among the people to purify them. The Lord's anger is raging, and a plague already started!'
16.47: Aaron did exactly what Moses said and ran out among the people. The plague had already begun, but Aaron burned the incense and purified the people.
16.48: He stood between the living and the dead, and the plague stopped.
16.49: But by then, 14,700 people had already died—on top of the ones who died with Korah's rebellion.
16.50: When the plague finally stopped, Aaron went back to Moses at the entrance of the Tabernacle.

17.2: 'Tell the Israelites to bring you twelve wooden staffs—one from each tribal leader. Write each leader's name on his staff.'
17.3: 'Write Aaron's name on the staff for the tribe of Levi, 'cause each ancestral tribe needs to have one staff.'
17.4: 'Put all the staffs inside the Tabernacle, in front of the Ark that holds the tablets of the Covenant, the spot where I meet with you.'
17.5: 'The staff of the man I choose gon' sprout buds. Then this gon' finally stop the people from whining and complaining against you.'
17.6: So Moses told the Israelites what the Lord said, and all twelve tribal leaders, including Aaron, brought their staffs to Moses.
17.7: Moses placed the staffs in the Tabernacle, right before the Lord.
17.8: The next day, Moses went into the Tabernacle and saw that Aaron's staff—representing the tribe of Levi—had sprouted! It had buds, blossoms, and even ripe almonds!
17.9: Moses brought all the staffs out from the Tabernacle and showed them to the people. Each leader took back his own staff.
17.10: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Take Aaron's staff and put it back in front of the Ark of the Covenant. Let it be a warning to all the rebels. This gon' put a stop to their complaining before they get themselves killed.'
17.11: So Moses did exactly what the Lord commanded him.
17.12: Then the Israelites said to Moses, 'Look, we doomed! We finished! We dead for sure!'
17.13: 'Anybody who even comes near the Lord's Tabernacle dies. Are we all about to die!?'

18.1: Then the Lord told Aaron, 'You, your sons, and your Levite relatives are responsible for any offenses related to the sanctuary. But only you and your sons are responsible for anything connected to the priesthood.'
18.2: 'Bring your relatives from the tribe of Levi to help you and your sons as y'all serve at the Tabernacle of the Covenant.'
18.3: 'The Levites gotta handle their assigned duties, but they can't go near the sacred objects or the altar—if they do, both you and them will die.'
18.4: 'The Levites gotta help you take care of the Tabernacle, but no unauthorized person can help with this work.'
18.5: 'Y'all gotta perform the sacred duties inside the sanctuary and at the altar. If you follow these instructions, the Lord's anger won't come against Israel again.'
18.6: 'I personally chose your fellow Levites from the Israelites to assist you. They're a gift to you, dedicated to the Lord's service.'
18.7: 'But you and your sons gotta handle everything related to the priesthood—the altar, the sacred items, and the duties behind the inner curtain. I'm giving y'all this responsibility as a privilege. Anybody who ain't authorized and tries to come near will be put to death.'
18.8: Then the Lord told Aaron, 'I'm putting you in charge of all the holy offerings the Israelites bring to me. These are yours and your sons' to keep forever.'
18.9: 'You get a share of all the most holy offerings that ain't burned up—the grain offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings. These belong to you and your sons.'
18.10: 'Y'all gotta eat them in a holy place. Only males can eat them, and you must treat them as sacred.'
18.11: 'Also, the sacred and special offerings the Israelites lift up belong to you. These are for you, your sons, and your daughters as a permanent share. Any family member who is ceremonially clean can eat them.'
18.12: 'I'm also giving you the first of the olive oil, new wine, and grain that the people bring as offerings to the Lord.'
18.13: 'Every first crop from the land that the people offer to the Lord belongs to you. Any family member who is clean can eat it.'
18.14: 'Anything in Israel that's set apart for the Lord belongs to you.'
18.15: 'Every firstborn—whether human or animal—that's given to the Lord is yours. But you gotta redeem the firstborn sons and any unclean animals.'
18.16: 'Redeem them when they a month old. The redemption price is five silver pieces (measured by the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs).'
18.17: 'But don't redeem firstborn cattle, sheep, or goats. They're holy and belong to the Lord. Sprinkle their blood on the altar and burn their fat as a special gift, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.'
18.18: 'The meat from these animals is yours, just like the breast and right thigh from the special offerings.'
18.19: 'I'm giving you all these holy offerings that the Israelites bring to the Lord. They're for you, your sons, and your daughters forever. This is an everlasting covenant between me, you, and your descendants.'
18.20: Then the Lord told Aaron, 'Y'all priests won't get no land or property like the other tribes. I am your share and your inheritance.'
18.21: 'As for the Levites, I'ma take care of them by giving them tithes from the Israelites instead of land.'
18.22: 'No Israelite (except priests and Levites) can come near the Tabernacle. If they do, they'll be guilty and die.'
18.23: 'Only the Levites can serve at the Tabernacle, and they'll be responsible for any offenses against it. This law is permanent. Levites won't get any land among the Israelites.'
18.24: 'Instead of land, I'm giving the Levites the Israelites' tithes, which are sacred offerings to the Lord. That's why they won't get land like the other tribes.'
18.26: 'Tell the Levites: When y'all receive tithes from the Israelites (which is your share), you gotta give a tenth of those tithes to the Lord as an offering.'
18.27: 'The Lord will count this offering as if it was your own grain or wine harvest.'
18.28: 'Give a tenth of the tithes y'all receive as a sacred offering to the Lord, and give it to Aaron the priest.'
18.29: 'Make sure y'all give the best portions of what y'all receive as an offering to the Lord.'
18.30: 'When you give your best portion, the rest of the tithes will be considered yours, just like if you grew them yourself.'
18.31: 'You and your families can eat this food wherever y'all want. It's your payment for serving in the Tabernacle.'
18.32: 'You won't be guilty for receiving the Lord's tithes as long as you give the best portion to the priests. But don't treat the holy gifts like they common—if you do, you'll die.'

19.1: Then the Lord told Moses and Aaron,
19.2: 'Here go another law y'all gotta follow: Tell the Israelites to bring a red heifer—a perfect one, no defects, and it can't have ever been used to pull a plow.'
19.3: 'Give it to Eleazar the priest. He gon' take it outside the camp and have it killed while he watches.'
19.4: 'Eleazar gon' dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the Tabernacle.'
19.5: 'Then, while Eleazar watches, the heifer gotta be burned—skin, meat, blood, and all.'
19.6: 'The priest gotta take some cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and some scarlet yarn, and throw 'em into the fire burning the heifer.'
19.7: 'Then the priest gotta wash his clothes and take a bath. After that, he can come back into the camp, but he still gon' be unclean till evening.'
19.8: 'The person who burned the animal gotta wash his clothes, take a bath, and he also gon' be unclean till evening.'
19.9: 'Then somebody who's already clean gotta collect the ashes from the heifer and store them in a purified place outside the camp. These ashes gon' be used to make the purification water for removing sin.'
19.10: 'The person who gathers the ashes gotta wash his clothes and stay unclean till evening. This law applies forever to the Israelites and even the foreigners living among y'all.'
19.11: 'Anybody who touches a dead body gon' be unclean for seven days.'
19.12: 'On the third and seventh days, they gotta wash themselves with the purification water to get clean. If they don't, they still gon' be unclean even after the seventh day.'
19.13: 'Anybody who touches a dead body and don't cleanse themselves properly messes up the Lord's Tabernacle. They gotta be cut off from the community. If they ain't sprinkled with the purification water, they still dirty.'
19.14: 'Here's the rule when somebody dies inside a tent: Everybody inside, plus anybody who walks into that tent, gon' be unclean for seven days.'
19.15: 'Any open container in that tent with no lid on it is unclean too.'
19.16: 'If somebody touches a dead body out in an open field—whether the person was killed or just died naturally—or if they touch a human bone or a grave, they unclean for seven days.'
19.17: 'To cleanse them, take some of the ashes from the burnt purification offering and put them in a jar. Then pour fresh water over them.'
19.18: 'Somebody who's already clean gotta take a hyssop branch, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it over the tent, the furniture, and everybody who was inside. Also sprinkle it on anybody who touched a human bone, a dead body, or a grave.'
19.19: 'On the third and seventh days, the clean person gotta sprinkle the purification water on the unclean people. Then on the seventh day, those being cleansed gotta wash their clothes and take a bath. That evening, they'll finally be clean.'
19.20: 'But if somebody refuses to purify themselves, they gotta be cut off from the community 'cause they defiling the Lord's sanctuary. If they ain't been sprinkled with the purification water, they still unclean.'
19.21: 'This rule lasts forever. Anybody who sprinkles the purification water gotta wash their clothes afterward, and anybody who touches that water is unclean till evening.'
19.22: 'Anything or anybody touched by someone unclean is also unclean till evening.'

20.1: In the first month of the year, the whole Israelite community reached the wilderness of Zin and set up camp at Kadesh. While they was there, Miriam died and was buried.
20.2: Ain't no water for the people to drink, so they started turning against Moses and Aaron.
20.3: The people blamed Moses, saying, 'Man, we shoulda just died when our brothers did in the Lord's presence!'
20.4: 'Why you bring the Lord's people out here in the wilderness to die, along with all our animals?'
20.5: 'Why you make us leave Egypt just to bring us to this awful place? Ain't no grain, no figs, no grapes, no pomegranates—ain't even no water to drink!'
20.6: Moses and Aaron left the people and went to the entrance of the Tabernacle. They fell face down, and the Lord's presence appeared to them.
20.8: 'Take the staff, gather the whole community, and in front of everybody, speak to that rock over there. It gon' pour out water, and y'all will have enough for the whole community and all the animals.'
20.9: So Moses did what he was told—he grabbed the staff from its place before the Lord.
20.10: Then he and Aaron called the people together at the rock. Moses shouted, 'Listen up, you rebels! Do we gotta bring water out this rock for y'all?'
20.11: Then Moses raised his hand and hit the rock twice with the staff. Water gushed out, and the whole community, along with their animals, drank all they wanted.
20.12: But the Lord told Moses and Aaron, 'Y'all ain't trust me enough to show my holiness to the people. Because of that, y'all ain't leading them into the land I'm giving them.'
20.13: That place was called Meribah (which means 'arguing') 'cause that's where the Israelites argued with the Lord, and He showed His holiness there.
20.14: While Moses was still at Kadesh, he sent messengers to the king of Edom with this message:
20.15: 'This what your relatives, the Israelites, gotta say: You know all the trouble we been through.'
20.16: 'Our ancestors went down to Egypt, and we stayed there for a long time. But the Egyptians treated us bad—real bad.'
20.17: 'When we cried out to the Lord, He heard us and sent an angel to bring us outta Egypt. Now we right here at Kadesh, on the border of your land.'
20.18: 'Please let us pass through. We ain't gon' go through no fields or vineyards, and we won't drink none of your well water. We'll stay on the king's road till we outta your land.'
20.19: But the king of Edom said, 'Nah, stay out my land, or I'ma meet y'all with an army!'
20.20: The Israelites said, 'We'll stay on the road. If our animals drink any of your water, we'll pay for it. Just let us pass, that's all we asking.'
20.21: But the king of Edom said, 'I SAID NO!' Then he brought out his whole army, ready for war.
20.22: Since Edom refused to let Israel pass through their land, the Israelites had to turn around and go another way.
20.23: The whole Israelite community left Kadesh and traveled to Mount Hor.
20.24: At the border of Edom, the Lord told Moses and Aaron,
20.25: 'Aaron's time is up. He about to die. He ain't going into the land I promised the Israelites 'cause both of y'all went against my instructions at Meribah.'
20.26: 'Take Aaron and his son Eleazar up Mount Hor.'
20.27: 'Take off Aaron's priestly clothes and put them on Eleazar. Aaron gon' die up there and join his ancestors.'
20.28: So Moses did what the Lord commanded. He, Aaron, and Eleazar climbed Mount Hor while everybody watched.
20.29: At the top of the mountain, Moses took off Aaron's priestly garments and put them on Eleazar. Then Aaron died right there on the mountain, and Moses and Eleazar came back down.
20.30: When the people saw that Aaron was dead, the whole Israelite community mourned for him thirty days.

21.1: The king of Arad, a Canaanite who lived in the Negev, heard the Israelites was coming through Atharim. So he attacked them and took some people as prisoners.
21.2: Then Israel made a vow to the Lord: 'If you let us win against them, we gon' destroy all their towns.'
21.3: The Lord heard them and gave them victory over the Canaanites. They destroyed them and their towns completely, and that place been called Hormah ever since.
21.4: The Israelites left Mount Hor, taking the road toward the Red Sea to go around Edom. But the journey was long, and they got impatient.
21.5: They started complaining against God and Moses: 'Why you bring us out of Egypt just to die out here in the wilderness? Ain't no food, no water, and we sick of this nasty manna!'
21.6: So the Lord sent poisonous snakes among them, and a lot of people got bit and died.
21.7: Then the people ran to Moses and cried out, 'We messed up! We spoke against the Lord and against you. Please pray to the Lord to take away these snakes!' So Moses prayed for them.
21.8: The Lord told Moses, 'Make a copy of a poisonous snake and put it on a pole. Whoever gets bit and looks at it will live.'
21.9: So Moses made a bronze snake and put it on a pole. Whenever somebody got bit, if they looked at the bronze snake, they got healed.
21.10: The Israelites traveled to Oboth and camped there.
21.11: Then they moved to Iye-abarim, in the wilderness on the eastern border of Moab.
21.12: From there, they set up camp in the valley of Zered Brook.
21.13: Then they moved again and camped on the far side of the Arnon River, near the Amorite territory. The Arnon River was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
21.14: That's why The Book of the Wars of the Lord talks about: 'Waheb in Suphah and the ravines of the Arnon River,'
21.15: 'And the valleys that stretch to Ar, near Moab's border.'
21.16: From there, Israel went to Beer, the well where the Lord told Moses, 'Gather the people—I'ma give them water.'
21.17: There, the Israelites sang: 'Spring up, O well! Yes, sing its praises!'
21.18: 'Sing about the well, the one princes dug, the one leaders hollowed out with their staffs and scepters.'
21.19: Then they left the wilderness and traveled through Mattanah,
21.20: Then through Nahaliel and Bamoth, and finally to the valley in Moab, where Pisgah Peak overlooks the desert.
21.21: Israel sent messengers to King Sihon of the Amorites with a message:
21.22: 'Let us pass through your land. We won't touch your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink from your wells. We gon' stay on the main road till we outta your territory.'
21.23: But King Sihon said, 'Nah, y'all ain't passing through here.' Instead, he gathered his whole army and attacked Israel in the wilderness at Jahaz.
21.24: But Israel wiped them out with the sword and took their land from the Arnon River to the Jabbok River, stopping at the Ammonite border, 'cause that place was well-defended.
21.25: Israel captured all the Amorite towns and settled in them, including Heshbon and the nearby villages.
21.26: Heshbon was King Sihon's capital. He had taken it from the Moabite king before, seizing everything up to the Arnon River.
21.27: That's why the old poets wrote: 'Come to Heshbon! Rebuild it! Let Sihon's city be restored!'
21.28: 'A fire came from Heshbon, a flame from Sihon's city! It burned down Ar in Moab, destroying the Arnon rulers!'
21.29: 'Moab, y'all in trouble! Your god Chemosh failed y'all! He let y'all sons become refugees and y'all daughters be taken captive by Sihon, the Amorite king.'
21.30: 'We crushed 'em from Heshbon to Dibon, we wiped 'em out as far as Nophah and Medeba!'
21.31: So Israel took over the Amorite land.
21.32: Then Moses sent spies to scout out Jazer. Israel captured it and drove out the Amorites living there.
21.33: Next, they turned toward Bashan, but King Og of Bashan and his whole army attacked them at Edrei.
21.34: The Lord told Moses, 'Don't be scared of him. I already handed him over to you, along with his people and land. Do to him what you did to King Sihon of the Amorites.'
