21.35: So Israel killed King Og, his sons, and all his people—nobody survived. Then Israel took over his land too.

22.1: The Israelites traveled to the plains of Moab and camped east of the Jordan River, across from Jericho.
22.2: Balak, son of Zippor, the king of Moab, saw everything Israel did to the Amorites.
22.3: When Moab saw how many Israelites there were, they got shook. The people were terrified.
22.4: The king of Moab told the elders of Midian, 'Man, these folks 'bout to eat up everything like an ox eats grass!'
22.5: So Balak, king of Moab, sent messengers to Balaam (son of Beor), who was living in Pethor near the Euphrates River. The message said:
22.6: 'Look, a huge crowd of people just came from Egypt, and they covering the whole land. They a threat to me!'
22.7: 'Please come curse them for me! They too strong for me to handle. Maybe if you curse them, I can fight them off and kick them outta here. I know that whoever you bless gets blessed, and whoever you curse gets cursed.'
22.8: The messengers (elders from Moab and Midian) came with money to pay Balaam to curse Israel. They told him Balak's message.
22.9: Balaam told them, 'Stay here overnight. I'ma see what the Lord say to me in the morning.' So the officials stayed the night with Balaam.
22.10: That night, God came to Balaam and asked, 'Who these men staying with you?'
22.11: Balaam said, 'Balak, king of Moab, sent me a message saying:'
22.12: 'A crowd came outta Egypt, they covering the whole land. He wants me to curse them so he can fight them off.'
22.13: But God told Balaam, 'Don't go with them. You not gon' curse these people—'cause they already blessed!'
22.14: The next morning, Balaam told Balak's officials, 'Y'all gotta head home. The Lord won't let me go with y'all.'
22.15: So the Moabite officials went back to Balak and told him what Balaam said.
22.16: Balak wasn't giving up. He sent more officials, this time even more important ones.
22.17: They went to Balaam and said, 'Balak said: Please don't let nothing stop you from coming to help me.'
22.18: 'I'll pay you well, whatever you ask. Just come curse these people for me!'
22.19: Balaam answered, 'Even if Balak gave me his whole palace full of silver and gold, I couldn't go against the Lord.'
22.20: 'But stay here one more night, and I'ma see if the Lord got something else to say to me.'
22.21: That night, God told Balaam, 'Since these men came for you, go with them. But only say what I tell you to say.'
22.22: The next morning, Balaam got up, saddled his donkey, and left with Balak's officials. But God was mad that Balaam was going, so He sent an angel to block his way.
22.23: Balaam and two of his servants were riding along when the donkey saw the angel standing in the road with a sword drawn. The donkey swerved off the road into a field, but Balaam beat it and forced it back onto the path.
22.24: Then the angel stood where the road narrowed between two vineyard walls.
22.25: The donkey saw the angel again, tried to squeeze past, and crushed Balaam's foot against the wall. Balaam got mad and beat the donkey again.
22.26: The angel moved again and stood in a spot where there was no way to pass.
22.27: This time, the donkey straight up lay down under Balaam. Balaam lost his temper and started beating the donkey with his staff.
22.28: Then the Lord made the donkey talk! It said, 'What I do to you that made you beat me three times?'
22.29: Balaam shouted, 'You made me look stupid! If I had a sword, I'd kill you right now!'
22.30: The donkey said, 'Bruh, I been your ride all these years. Have I ever acted like this before?'
22.32: Then the Lord opened Balaam's eyes. He saw the angel of the Lord standing there with a sword drawn. Balaam fell face down in fear.
22.33: The angel said, 'Why you beat your donkey three times? I came to block your way 'cause you acting reckless against me.'
22.34: 'Your donkey saw me and moved three times—if it hadn't, I woulda killed you already and let the donkey live!'
22.35: Balaam said, 'I messed up. I ain't realize you was blocking me. If you don't want me to go, I'll turn around.'
22.36: The angel of the Lord told Balaam, 'Nah, go ahead with them. But remember—you only say what I tell you to say.' So Balaam kept going with Balak's officials.
22.37: When Balak heard Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at a Moabite town on the Arnon River, right at the edge of his land.
22.38: Balak said, 'Didn't I send for you? Why you ain't come right away? You ain't believe me when I said I'd pay you good?'
22.39: Balaam said, 'Look, I'm here now, but I can't say whatever I want. I'ma only say what God tells me to say.'
22.40: Then Balaam went with Balak to Kiriath-huzoth. Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and sent some of the meat to Balaam and the officials.
22.41: The next morning, Balak took Balaam up to Bamoth-baal, where he could see some of the Israelites camped below.

23.1: Then Balaam told King Balak, 'Build me seven altars right here, and bring seven young bulls and seven rams for sacrifice.'
23.2: Balak did exactly what Balaam said, and they sacrificed a young bull and a ram on each altar.
23.3: Then Balaam told Balak, 'Stand here by your burnt offerings, and I'ma go see if the Lord got something to say to me. Whatever He tell me, I'ma let you know.' Then Balaam went up to a bare hill.
23.4: God met Balaam there, and Balaam said, 'Lord, I set up seven altars and sacrificed a young bull and a ram on each one.'
23.5: Then the Lord gave Balaam a message and said, 'Go back to Balak and tell him exactly what I said.'
23.6: So Balaam went back and found Balak standing next to the burnt offerings with all the Moabite officials.
23.7: Then Balaam gave this message: 'Balak brought me from Aram, The king of Moab called me from the east. He said, "Come curse Jacob for me! Come put down Israel!"'
23.8: 'But how can I curse who God ain't cursed? How can I condemn who the Lord ain't condemned?'
23.9: 'I see them from the high places, I watch them from the hills. These people different— They set apart from the rest of the nations.'
23.10: 'Who can count Jacob's people? They as numerous as the dust! Who can even count a fourth of Israel? Let me die like the righteous, Let my life end like theirs!'
23.11: Then Balak got mad and said, 'What you doing?! I brought you here to curse my enemies, not bless them!'
23.12: But Balaam said, 'I can only speak what the Lord put in my mouth.'
23.13: Then Balak said, 'Come with me to another spot. You won't see all of them, but at least curse the ones you can see!'
23.14: So Balak took Balaam to Zophim on Pisgah Peak. He built seven altars there and offered a young bull and a ram on each altar.
23.15: Then Balaam told Balak, 'Stand here by your burnt offerings while I go meet the Lord again.'
23.16: The Lord met Balaam and gave him another message. Then He said, 'Go back to Balak and tell him this.'
23.17: So Balaam went back and found Balak standing beside his burnt offerings with all his officials. Balak asked, 'Well? What did the Lord say?'
23.18: Then Balaam said: 'Get up, Balak, and listen! Hear me, son of Zippor!'
23.19: 'God ain't human, so He don't lie. He don't change His mind like people do. If He say something, He gon' do it. If He make a promise, He gon' keep it.'
23.20: 'Listen, I got a command to bless— God already blessed them, And I can't take that back!'
23.21: 'Ain't no disaster planned for Jacob. Ain't no trouble waiting for Israel. The Lord their God is with them, They know He is their King.'
23.22: 'God brought them outta Egypt, And He as strong as a wild ox for them.'
23.23: 'Ain't no curse that can touch Jacob! Ain't no magic that got power over Israel! People gon' say, "Look at what God did for them!"'
23.24: 'These people rise up like a lioness, Like a lion waking up, ready to hunt. They won't rest Till they feasting on their prey, Drinking the blood of the slaughtered!'
23.25: Balak said to Balaam, 'Alright, fine! If you won't curse them, at least stop blessing them!'
23.26: But Balaam replied, 'Didn't I tell you? I can only say what the Lord tells me to say!'
23.27: Then Balak said, 'Come on, I'ma take you to one more place. Maybe God will let you curse them from there.'
23.28: So Balak took Balaam to Mount Peor, overlooking the wasteland.
23.29: Balaam told Balak, 'Build me seven altars and get seven young bulls and seven rams for me to sacrifice.'
23.30: So Balak did what Balaam said, and he sacrificed a young bull and a ram on each altar.

24.1: By now, Balaam knew for sure the Lord was set on blessing Israel, so this time, he ain't even try no divination. Instead, he turned toward the wilderness.
24.2: He looked out and saw Israel camped, tribe by tribe. Then the Spirit of God took over him.
24.3: This what Balaam, son of Beor, had to say: 'The message from the man who see things clear,'
24.4: 'The one who hear God's words, Who see visions from the Almighty, Who bow down with eyes wide open.'
24.5: 'Jacob, your tents look real good! Israel, your homes look lovely!'
24.6: 'Y'all spread out like palm groves, Like gardens by the river, Like tall trees planted by the Lord, Like cedars beside the water.'
24.7: 'Water flows freely for y'all, Y'all kids gon' have everything they need. Y'all king gon' be greater than Agag, Y'all kingdom gon' be lifted up.'
24.8: 'God brought them outta Egypt, And He strong like a wild ox for them. They tear up any nation that stand against them, Breaking bones, Shooting arrows that don't miss.'
24.9: 'Like a lion, Israel crouches and rests; Like a lioness, who bold enough to wake 'em up? Blessed is everybody who bless y'all, Israel, And cursed is everybody who curse y'all!'
24.10: Balak was heated. He clapped his hands in anger and yelled at Balaam, 'I brought you here to curse my enemies, and all you done is bless them three times!'
24.11: 'Now get outta here! Go home! I was finna pay you good, but the Lord done blocked you from getting rich!'
24.12: Balaam told Balak, 'You acting like I ain't tell your messengers the deal already…'
24.13: 'Even if Balak gave me his whole palace full of silver and gold, I still wouldn't be able to go against what the Lord say! I told you—I can only say what the Lord tell me to say.'
24.14: 'Now I'm going home. But before I leave, let me tell you what Israel finna do to your people in the future.'
24.15: Then Balaam gave another prophecy: 'This from Balaam, son of Beor, The man who see things clear.'
24.16: 'The one who hear God's words, Who got knowledge from the Most High, Who see visions from the Almighty, Who bow down with eyes wide open.'
24.17: 'I see him, but he ain't here yet. I can see him, but he still far in the future. A star gon' rise from Jacob; A ruler gon' come outta Israel. He gon' crush the heads of Moab, Smashing the skulls of Sheth's people.'
24.18: 'Edom gon' be taken over, Seir gon' be conquered, While Israel keep marching strong.'
24.19: 'A ruler gon' rise from Jacob, And he gon' wipe out the last survivors of Ir.'
24.20: Then Balaam looked toward the Amalekites and said: 'Amalek was once the biggest nation, But in the end, they gon' be wiped out!'
24.21: Then he looked over at the Kenites and said: 'Y'all got a safe home, Set up high in the rocks.'
24.22: 'But even y'all ain't safe forever— Assyria gon' take y'all captive!'
24.23: Then Balaam gave his last message: 'Man, who can survive If God say otherwise?'
24.24: 'Ships gon' come from Cyprus, They gon' bring trouble to Assyria, And they gon' afflict Eber, But even they gon' end up destroyed.'
24.25: Then Balaam packed up and went home. And Balak went his own way too.

25.1: While the Israelites was camped at Acacia Grove, some of the men messed up by sleeping with the Moabite women in the area.
25.2: These women invited them to their sacrifices for their gods, and the Israelites went along, eating with them and worshiping the gods of Moab.
25.3: That's how Israel ended up worshiping Baal of Peor, and the Lord got real mad at His people.
25.4: The Lord told Moses, 'Grab all the ringleaders and execute them in broad daylight. That way, my anger will turn away from Israel.'
25.5: So Moses told Israel's judges, 'Each of y'all gotta put to death the men under you who bowed down to Baal of Peor.'
25.6: Right then, an Israelite man walked up bold as ever with a Midianite woman and took her into his tent, right in front of Moses and everybody else, while folks was crying at the Tabernacle entrance.
25.7: When Phinehas, son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron the priest, saw this, he jumped up and grabbed his spear.
25.8: He ran straight into the tent and stabbed the man through his body, and the spear went all the way through into the woman's stomach. Right then, the plague on Israel stopped.
25.9: But by that time, 24,000 people had already died from it.
25.11: 'Phinehas, son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron the priest, turned my anger away from the Israelites. He was as zealous as I was, so I didn't wipe out Israel like I was about to.'
25.12: 'Now tell him I'm making a special covenant of peace with him.'
25.13: 'From now on, him and his descendants got a permanent right to the priesthood, 'cause he stood up for me and purified the Israelites, making them right with me again.'
25.14: The Israelite man who got killed with the Midianite woman was Zimri, son of Salu, a leader from the tribe of Simeon.
25.15: The woman's name was Cozbi, daughter of Zur, a leader from a Midianite clan.
25.17: 'Go attack the Midianites and destroy them!'
25.18: 'They deceived y'all and tricked you into worshiping Baal of Peor. Plus, Cozbi—the Midianite leader's daughter—was the reason y'all fell into sin. She got killed when that plague hit y'all at Peor.'

26.1: After the plague ended, the Lord spoke to Moses and Eleazar, Aaron's son, the priest.
26.2: He said, 'Count up all the folks in Israel, twenty years old and up, by their families—everybody who can fight in war.'
26.3: So Moses and Eleazar the priest talked to the people while they were camped in the plains of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho.
26.4: They said, 'Y'all gotta count everybody twenty and older, just like the Lord told Moses. That includes everybody who came up outta Egypt.'
26.5: Reuben was Israel's firstborn. These the families that came from Reuben: Hanoch—which became the Hanochite family. Pallu—which became the Palluite family.
26.6: Hezron—which became the Hezronite family. Carmi—which became the Carmite family.
26.7: These were the families of Reuben, and their total warriors came to 43,730.
26.8: Pallu had a son named Eliab.
26.9: Eliab's sons were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These the same Dathan and Abiram who went against Moses and Aaron, leading the rebellion with Korah when they went against the Lord.
26.10: The earth straight-up opened its mouth and swallowed them and Korah's whole crew when they died. Fire came down and burned up 250 men—and that became a warning for everybody.
26.11: But Korah's kids ain't die that day.
26.12: The sons of Simeon came from these families: Nemuel—which became the Nemuelite family. Jamin—which became the Jaminite family. Jachin—which became the Jachinite family.
26.13: Zerah—which became the Zarhite family. Shaul—which became the Shaulite family.
26.14: These were the families from Simeon, and their total warriors came to 22,200.
26.15: The sons of Gad came from these families: Zephon—which became the Zephonite family. Haggi—which became the Haggite family. Shuni—which became the Shunite family.
26.16: Ozni—which became the Oznite family. Eri—which became the Erite family.
26.17: Arod—which became the Arodite family. Areli—which became the Arelite family.
26.18: These were the families from Gad, and their total warriors came to 40,500.
26.19: Judah had two sons, Er and Onan, but both of them died back in Canaan.
26.20: The families that came from Judah's surviving sons were: Shelah—which became the Shelanite family. Perez—which became the Perezite family. Zerah—which became the Zarhite family.
26.21: The sons of Perez were: Hezron—which became the Hezronite family; Hamul—which became the Hamulite family.
26.22: These were the families from Judah, and their total warriors came to 76,500.
26.23: The sons of Issachar came from these families: Tola—which became the Tolaite family; Puah—which became the Punite family.
26.24: Jashub—which became the Jashubite family; Shimron—which became the Shimronite family.
26.25: These were the families from Issachar, and their total warriors came to 64,300.
26.26: The sons of Zebulun came from these families: Sered—which became the Sardite family; Elon—which became the Elonite family; Jahleel—which became the Jahleelite family.
26.27: These were the families from Zebulun, and their total warriors came to 60,500.
26.28: The sons of Joseph were split into the families of Manasseh and Ephraim.
26.29: The sons of Manasseh were: Machir—which became the Machirite family. Machir had a son named Gilead, which became the Gileadite family.
26.30: The sons of Gilead were: Jeezer—which became the Jeezerite family; Helek—which became the Helekite family.
26.31: Asriel—which became the Asrielite family; Shechem—which became the Shechemite family.
26.32: Shemida—which became the Shemidaite family; Hepher—which became the Hepherite family.
26.33: Zelophehad, son of Hepher, ain't have no sons, only daughters. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
26.34: These were the families from Manasseh, and their total warriors came to 52,700.
26.35: The sons of Ephraim came from these families: Shuthelah—which became the Shuthelahite family; Becher—which became the Bachrite family; Tahan—which became the Tahanite family.
26.36: The sons of Shuthelah were: Eran—which became the Eranite family.
26.37: These were the families from Ephraim, and their total warriors came to 32,500. These are the sons of Joseph, divided by their families.
26.38: The sons of Benjamin came from these families: Bela—which became the Belaite family; Ashbel—which became the Ashbelite family; Ahiram—which became the Ahiramite family.
26.39: Shupham—which became the Shuphamite family; Hupham—which became the Huphamite family.
26.40: The sons of Bela were: Ard—which became the Ardite family; Naaman—which became the Naamite family.
26.41: These the sons of Benjamin, grouped by their families. The total number of warriors from them was 45,600.
26.42: These the sons of Dan, grouped by their families: Shuham—which became the Shuhamite family. These the families of Dan, grouped by their families.
26.43: All the Shuhamite families together had a total of 64,400 warriors.
26.44: The sons of Asher, grouped by their families, were: Jimna—which became the Jimnite family. Jesui—which became the Jesuite family. Beriah—which became the Beriite family.
26.45: The sons of Beriah were: Heber—which became the Heberite family. Malchiel—which became the Malchielite family.
26.46: Asher also had a daughter named Serah.
26.47: These were the families from Asher, and their total warriors came to 53,400.
26.48: The sons of Naphtali, grouped by their families, were: Jahzeel—which became the Jahzeelite family. Guni—which became the Gunite family.
26.49: Jezer—which became the Jezerite family. Shillem—which became the Shillemite family.
26.50: These were the families from Naphtali, and their total warriors came to 45,400.
26.51: These were all the warriors counted from the children of Israel: 601,730.
26.52: Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
26.53: 'Y'all gon' split this land up between the tribes based on how many folks they got.'
26.54: 'The bigger tribes get more land, and the smaller ones get less. Everybody gets a share based on their numbers.'
26.55: 'But listen—y'all gotta split the land by casting lots. That way, everybody gets what they supposed to, based on their family's name.'
26.56: 'Whether they a big tribe or a small one, the land they get will be decided by the lot.'
26.57: These the families of the Levites, counted by their clans: Gershon—which became the Gershonite family. Kohath—which became the Kohathite family. Merari—which became the Merarite family.
26.58: Other Levite families: Libnites, Hebronites, Mahlites, Mushites, and Korahites. Kohath was the father of Amram.
26.59: Amram's wife was named Jochebed—she was the daughter of Levi, born to Levi in Egypt. She gave birth to Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam.
26.60: Aaron had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
26.61: Now Nadab and Abihu got killed when they messed up and brought some profane fire before the Lord.
26.62: The total number of Levite males from one month old and up was 23,000. But they ain't get counted with the rest of Israel, 'cause they ain't get no land inheritance like the other tribes.
26.63: These the numbers counted by Moses and Eleazar the priest, when they counted the people of Israel in the plains of Moab, across the Jordan River from Jericho.
26.64: Ain't none of these folks part of the original group that Moses and Aaron counted when they did the first census back in the Wilderness of Sinai.
26.65: 'Cause the Lord had already said, 'They all gon' die in the wilderness.' And that's exactly what happened. Ain't nobody left from that first group—except for Caleb, son of Jephunneh, and Joshua, son of Nun.

27.1: Now here come Zelophehad's daughters—he was Hepher's son, Gilead's grandson, from Machir of Manasseh, from Joseph's family. Their names? Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
27.2: They pulled up on Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole congregation right at the entrance of the Tabernacle of Meeting and said—
27.3: 'Look, our daddy died out in the wilderness, but he ain't die in Korah's rebellion against the Lord. He died 'cause of his own sins, but he ain't have no sons.'
27.4: 'Why should our daddy's name just disappear from his family just 'cause he ain't have no sons? We should get some land too—give us a share among his brothers!'
27.5: So Moses took their case straight to the Lord.
27.7: 'Zelophehad's daughters speaking facts! They deserve land, just like their uncles. Give 'em a share of their daddy's inheritance.'
27.8: 'And tell Israel—if a man die and he ain't got no sons, his land go to his daughter.'
27.9: 'If he ain't got no daughter, give it to his brothers.'
27.10: 'If he ain't got no brothers, give it to his uncles.'
27.11: 'If his daddy ain't got no brothers, give it to his closest family member. That's how it's gotta be for all of Israel, 'cause the Lord said so.'
27.12: Then the Lord told Moses—'Go up this Mount Abarim and look at the land I'm giving Israel.'
27.13: 'Once you see it, you gon' be gathered with your people, just like your brother Aaron was.'
27.14: ''Cause back at Meribah, in the Wilderness of Zin, when the people was outta control, you ain't follow My command to show My holiness before their eyes. That's why.'
27.15: Then Moses spoke to the Lord and said—
27.16: 'Lord, You the God of all spirits, pick somebody to lead these people.'
27.17: 'Somebody to go out before 'em, lead 'em, bring 'em back—so they don't be like sheep with no shepherd.'
27.18: And the Lord told Moses—'Take Joshua, son of Nun, he got the Spirit in him. Lay your hands on him.'
27.19: 'Bring him in front of Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, and make it official in front of everybody.'
27.20: 'Give him some of your authority, so Israel will listen to him.'
27.21: 'He gon' stand before Eleazar the priest, who gon' ask the Lord what to do using the Urim (sacred dice). When Joshua say go, Israel move. When he say stop, they stay.'
27.22: So Moses did exactly what the Lord said. He brought Joshua before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation.
27.23: He laid his hands on him, put him in charge—just like the Lord told him to do.

28.2: 'Tell Israel this: My offerings, the food I want y'all to burn for Me, gotta be given at the right time, and y'all need to make sure y'all do it right.'
28.3: 'This what y'all gotta bring as a fire offering to the Lord—two male lambs, a year old, with no defects, every single day as a regular burnt offering.'
28.4: 'Offer one in the morning and the other in the evening.'
28.5: 'With it, bring one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour, mixed with a quarter hin of pressed olive oil as a grain offering.'
28.6: 'This burnt offering been required since Mount Sinai, and it's supposed to be a sweet-smelling sacrifice to the Lord, burned by fire.'
28.7: 'With each lamb, bring a drink offering—one-fourth of a hin of wine—and pour it out in the holy place for the Lord.'
28.8: 'At evening, offer the second lamb with the same grain offering and drink offering, just like in the morning. Let it be a fire offering with a sweet smell to the Lord.'
28.9: 'On the Sabbath, bring two lambs a year old, with no defects. Along with that, bring two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and the proper drink offering.'
28.10: 'That's the burnt offering for every Sabbath, on top of the daily burnt offering and its drink offering.'
28.11: 'At the start of each month, bring a burnt offering to the Lord—two young bulls, one ram, and seven lambs, all a year old and without defects.'
28.12: 'Each bull gotta have three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering. The ram gotta have two-tenths.'
28.13: 'Each lamb gotta have one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering. This is a burnt offering that smells real good to the Lord, a fire offering.'
28.14: 'For drink offerings—half a hin of wine for each bull, one-third of a hin for a ram, and one-fourth of a hin for a lamb. This burnt offering should happen every month, every year.'
28.15: 'And also bring one male goat as a sin offering to the Lord, along with the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.'
28.16: 'On the fourteenth day of the first month, that's the Passover for the Lord.'
28.17: 'On the fifteenth day, it's a feast. Y'all gotta eat unleavened bread for seven days.'
28.18: 'On the first day, have a holy gathering—don't do no regular work.'
28.19: 'Offer a burnt offering to the Lord—two young bulls, one ram, and seven lambs, all a year old, and make sure they got no defects.'
28.20: 'With them, bring fine flour mixed with oil—three-tenths of an ephah for each bull, and two-tenths for the ram.'
28.21: 'For each of the seven lambs, bring one-tenth of an ephah.'
28.22: 'Also, bring one male goat as a sin offering, to make things right for y'all.'
28.23: 'Offer these along with the morning burnt offering, which happens every day.'
28.24: 'For seven days, bring this food as a fire offering to the Lord, something that smells good to Him. Do this on top of the daily burnt offering and drink offering.'
28.25: 'And on the seventh day, have a holy gathering—don't do no regular work.'
28.26: 'On the day of Firstfruits, when y'all bring a new grain offering to the Lord at the Feast of Weeks, have a holy gathering—don't do no regular work.'
28.27: 'Offer a burnt offering with a sweet smell to the Lord—two young bulls, one ram, and seven lambs, all a year old.'
28.28: 'Bring fine flour mixed with oil for the grain offering—three-tenths of an ephah for each bull, two-tenths for the ram,'
28.29: 'And one-tenth for each of the seven lambs.'
28.30: 'Also, bring one male goat as a sin offering, to make things right for y'all.'
28.31: 'Make sure all these animals are perfect—no defects. Offer them along with their drink offerings, on top of the regular burnt offering and grain offering.'

29.1: On the first day of the seventh month, y'all need to have a holy gathering. Don't do no regular work, 'cause this the day to blow the trumpets.
29.2: Bring a burnt offering to the Lord—one young bull, one ram, and seven lambs, all a year old with no flaws.
29.3: The grain offering gotta be fine flour mixed with oil—three-tenths of an ephah for the bull, two-tenths for the ram,
29.4: And one-tenth for each of the seven lambs.
29.5: Also bring a male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for y'all.
29.6: Do all this alongside the burnt offering for the New Moon, the regular daily burnt offering, and their drink offerings, just like the Lord said. Let it be a fire offering with a sweet smell to the Lord.
29.7: On the tenth day of this seventh month, have a holy gathering. Y'all gotta humble yourselves—don't do no regular work.
29.8: Bring a burnt offering to the Lord that smells real good to Him—one young bull, one ram, and seven lambs, all a year old and without blemish.
29.9: The grain offering gotta be fine flour mixed with oil—three-tenths of an ephah for the bull, two-tenths for the ram,
29.10: And one-tenth for each of the seven lambs.
29.11: Also, bring a male goat as a sin offering, on top of the sin offering for atonement, the regular daily burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offerings.
29.12: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, have a holy gathering. Don't do no regular work, and y'all gotta keep a seven-day feast for the Lord.
29.13: Bring a burnt offering, a fire offering that smells good to the Lord—thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen lambs, all a year old and without no flaws.
29.14: The grain offering gotta be fine flour mixed with oil—three-tenths of an ephah for each of the thirteen bulls, two-tenths for each of the two rams,
29.15: And one-tenth for each of the fourteen lambs.
29.16: Also, bring a male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
29.17: On the second day, bring twelve bulls, two rams, and fourteen lambs, all a year old with no flaws.
29.18: Bring the right grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, just like the rules say.
29.19: Also, bring a male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
29.20: On the third day, bring eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen lambs, all a year old and without flaws.
29.21: Bring the right grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, just like the rules say.
29.22: Also, bring a male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
29.23: On the fourth day, bring ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen lambs, all a year old and without flaws.
29.24: Bring the right grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, just like the rules say.
29.25: Also, bring a male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
29.26: On the fifth day, bring nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen lambs, all a year old and without flaws.
29.27: Bring the right grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, just like the rules say.
29.28: Also, bring a male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
29.29: On the sixth day, bring eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen lambs, all a year old and without flaws.
29.30: Bring the right grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, just like the rules say.
29.31: Also, bring a male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
29.32: On the seventh day, bring seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen lambs, all a year old and without flaws.
29.33: Bring the right grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, just like the rules say.
29.34: Also, bring a male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
29.35: On the eighth day, have a sacred gathering. Don't do no regular work.
29.36: Bring a burnt offering, a fire offering that smells real good to the Lord—one bull, one ram, and seven lambs, all a year old and without flaws.
29.37: Bring the right grain and drink offerings for the bull, the ram, and the lambs, just like the rules say.
29.38: Also, bring a male goat as a sin offering, besides the regular burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
29.39: Y'all need to bring these offerings to the Lord at the right times, besides your own vowed offerings, freewill offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, and peace offerings.
29.40: And Moses told the people of Israel everything the Lord said, just like He commanded him.

30.1: Then Moses spoke to the leaders of the tribes of Israel, sayin', 'This what the Lord commanded:'
30.2: 'If a man make a vow to the Lord or swear an oath to bind hisself to a promise, he can't break his word. He gotta do everything he said he would.'
30.3: 'If a woman make a vow to the Lord while she still livin' in her daddy's house, and she promise somethin' serious,'
30.4: 'And her daddy hear about it and don't say nothin', then whatever she promised gon' stand, and she gotta keep it.'
30.5: 'But if her daddy step in that same day and say, 'Nah, I ain't lettin' that ride,' then her vow don't count, and the Lord will let her off the hook 'cause her daddy shut it down.'
30.6: 'Now, if she get married while she still got a vow or promise she made before she got a husband,'
30.7: 'And her husband hear about it and don't say nothin', then her vow gon' stand, and she gotta keep it.'
30.8: 'But if her husband shut it down that same day he hear it, then whatever she promised don't count, and the Lord gon' let her off the hook 'cause her husband overruled it.'
30.9: 'But if a woman a widow or divorced, whatever vow she make gon' stand—she gotta own up to it.'
30.10: 'If she make a vow while she livin' with her husband or promise somethin' serious,'
30.11: 'And her husband hear it and don't say nothin', then her vow gon' stand, and she gotta keep it.'
30.12: 'But if her husband step in and cancel it that same day, then whatever she said don't count, and the Lord gon' let her off the hook.'
30.13: 'Any vow or serious oath she take, her husband got the right to let it stand or shut it down.'
30.14: 'If her husband don't say nothin' day after day, then he confirmin' all her vows just by stayin' quiet—'cause he ain't stop it when he first heard it.'
30.15: 'But if he later try to cancel it after hearin' it before, then he gotta take responsibility for it.'
30.16: 'These the rules the Lord gave Moses, about vows between a husband and wife, and between a father and his daughter while she still livin' in his house.'

31.2: 'Go get payback on the Midianites for what they did to the Israelites. After that, you gon' be gathered with your ancestors.'
31.3: So Moses told the people, 'Get some of y'all ready for battle. Y'all gon' go fight against Midian to get revenge for the Lord.'
31.4: 'Send a thousand men from each tribe—twelve thousand in total—for the war.'
31.5: So they picked out one thousand men from each tribe, makin' twelve thousand warriors, all suited up for battle.
31.6: Moses sent 'em off to war, a thousand from each tribe, with Phinehas, Eleazar's son, leadin' the charge. Phinehas took the holy articles and the trumpets to sound the signals.
31.7: They went to war against Midian just like the Lord told Moses, and they wiped out all the men.
31.8: They killed the Midianite kings—Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba—five kings in total. They also took out Balaam, son of Beor, with the sword.
31.9: The Israelites took all the Midianite women and kids as prisoners. They also took their cattle, flocks, and all their goods as spoils of war.
31.10: They burned down every Midianite city and all their forts.
31.11: They grabbed everything—people, animals, and valuables—as plunder.
31.12: Then they brought all the captives, loot, and spoils back to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the whole Israelite congregation, settin' up camp on the plains of Moab by the Jordan River, right across from Jericho.
31.13: Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the people went out the camp to meet 'em.
31.14: But Moses was mad at the officers of the army—the commanders over thousands and hundreds—who came back from the battle.
31.15: Moses said, 'Y'all kept all these women alive?'
31.16: 'Don't y'all see? These the same women that led Israel into sin on Balaam's advice! That's why we got hit with that plague back at Peor!'
31.17: 'Now listen, kill all the little boys and every woman who done been with a man before.'
31.18: 'But keep all the young girls who ain't been with a man for yourselves.'
31.19: 'And for y'all who fought, stay outside the camp for seven days. Anybody who killed someone or even touched a dead body, y'all gotta cleanse yourselves and the captives on the third and seventh day.'
31.20: 'Y'all gotta purify every piece of clothing, everything made from leather, anything woven with goat hair, and all wooden objects.'
31.21: Then Eleazar the priest spoke to the soldiers who had fought, 'This the rule the Lord gave Moses:'
31.22: 'Gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, and lead—'
31.23: 'Anything that can take the heat, y'all gotta put it through fire to cleanse it. Then purify it with the special water. But if it can't survive fire, run it through water instead.'
31.24: 'Y'all also need to wash y'all clothes on the seventh day, then y'all can come back in the camp.'
31.26: 'Count up all the plunder—people and animals—you, Eleazar the priest, and the tribal leaders.'
31.27: 'Split it up two ways: half for the soldiers who fought, and half for everybody else in the camp.'
31.28: 'Take one outta every 500 from the soldiers' half—whether people, cattle, donkeys, or sheep—and give that to Eleazar the priest as an offering to the Lord.'
31.29: 'And from the Israelites' half, take one outta every 50 and give 'em to the Levites who take care of the Lord's tabernacle.'
31.30: 'Do this with all the people and animals taken as loot.'
31.31: So Moses and Eleazar did exactly what the Lord commanded.
31.32: The total loot from what the soldiers took in battle was 675,000 sheep,
31.35: And 32,000 young women who hadn't been with a man before.
31.36: From the soldiers' half, they got 337,500 sheep,
31.37: Outta that, the Lord's tribute was 675 sheep.
31.38: They had 36,000 cattle, and the Lord's tribute was 72.
31.39: They had 30,500 donkeys, and the Lord's tribute was 61.
31.40: And outta the 16,000 people, the Lord's tribute was 32 women.
31.41: Moses gave the tribute, the special offering to the Lord, to Eleazar the priest, just like the Lord commanded.
31.42: Then Moses divided up the Israelites' half,
31.43: And their share came to 337,500 sheep,
31.47: From that half, Moses took one outta every 50 people and animals and gave 'em to the Levites, just like the Lord commanded.
31.48: Then the officers who led the army—the commanders of thousands and hundreds—came to Moses.
31.49: They told him, 'We did a headcount of all the soldiers under us, and not a single one of us is missing.'
31.50: 'So we brought a gift for the Lord, everything we found—gold bracelets, chains, rings, earrings, and necklaces—to make atonement for ourselves before the Lord.'
31.51: So Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from them—all the fine jewelry.
31.52: The total gold offering given to the Lord by the army commanders was 16,750 shekels.
31.53: (Each soldier had already taken loot for themselves.)
31.54: Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from the commanders and brought it into the tabernacle as a memorial for the Israelites before the Lord.

32.1: Now the tribes of Reuben and Gad had a whole lotta livestock, and when they saw that the lands of Jazer and Gilead had good grazing spots, they knew it was perfect for their animals.
32.2: So the folks from Gad and Reuben went up to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of Israel, and said,
32.3: 'We talkin' 'bout Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Shebam, Nebo, and Beon—'
32.4: 'That land the Lord gave us when He handled those folks before Israel? That land is perfect for our livestock, and we got livestock.'
32.5: 'So if we good in your eyes, let us have this land as our inheritance. We don't wanna cross over the Jordan.'
32.6: Moses looked at the folks from Gad and Reuben and said, 'Hold up, so y'all just gon' sit here while your brothers out there fightin' for the land?'
32.7: 'Why y'all tryna make the rest of Israel lose heart about goin' into the land the Lord already gave them?'
32.8: 'This the same thing y'all fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-Barnea to spy out the land.'
32.9: 'They went up, saw the Valley of Eshcol, and instead of encouragin' everybody, they had folks scared to go claim what the Lord promised them.'
32.10: 'That's why the Lord got mad that day and swore an oath, sayin','
32.11: 'Ain't none of the folks who came up outta Egypt, twenty years and older, gon' see the land I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, 'cause they ain't really followed Me.'
32.12: 'Except Caleb, Jephunneh's son, from the Kenizzite clan, and Joshua, Nun's son—'cause they stayed loyal to Me.'
32.13: 'So the Lord got mad and made Israel wander the wilderness forty years 'til that whole generation of wicked folk was gone.'
32.14: 'And now, look at y'all! Y'all just like 'em, comin' up tryin' to test the Lord's patience and make Him even madder with Israel!'
32.15: 'If y'all turn away from Him again, He gon' leave these folks in the wilderness, and this whole nation gon' get wiped out.'
32.16: But they came closer to Moses and said, 'Look, we ain't tryna do all that. We gon' build sheep pens for our animals and cities for our families right here.'
32.17: 'But don't get it twisted, we gon' be suited up, ready to ride out ahead of the rest of Israel, leadin' the way 'til everybody got their land. Our families gon' stay in these fortified cities, safe from the people still in the land.'
32.18: 'We ain't even thinkin' 'bout comin' back home 'til every Israelite got their inheritance.'
32.19: 'See, we ain't tryna get no land on the other side of the Jordan, 'cause our inheritance is right here on this side.'
32.20: So Moses told them, 'Aight, if y'all serious about this—if y'all get suited up, ready for war before the Lord—'
32.21: 'And if all your armed men cross the Jordan ahead of the rest of Israel and fight 'til the Lord clears the land—'
32.22: 'Then y'all good. Y'all ain't got nothin' to worry about, and this land gon' be yours before the Lord.'
32.23: 'But if y'all don't do what y'all said, best believe y'all sinnin' against the Lord, and trust me, that sin gon' catch up to you.'
32.24: 'Go ahead, build your cities for your families and pens for your sheep—but make sure you do what you said you would.'
32.25: Then the folks from Gad and Reuben told Moses, 'Aight, we gon' do what you say.'
32.26: 'Our kids, wives, flocks, and livestock gon' stay here in Gilead.'
32.27: 'But every last one of us able to fight gon' cross the Jordan fully armed and ready for battle, just like you said, Moses.'
32.28: So Moses gave orders about them to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the Israelite tribes.
32.29: Moses said, 'If Gad and Reuben's men cross the Jordan armed for battle and fight with y'all till the land is secured, then they can keep Gilead as their own.'
32.30: 'But if they don't go with y'all into battle, then they gotta settle among y'all in Canaan.'
32.31: The people of Gad and Reuben said, 'We hear you. Whatever the Lord says, that's what we doin'.'
32.32: 'We gon' cross over armed and ready for battle before the Lord, but our inheritance gon' stay on this side of the Jordan.'
32.33: So Moses gave Gad, Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh (Joseph's son) the kingdoms of Sihon, king of the Amorites, and Og, king of Bashan—all the land, cities, and surrounding territory.
32.34: The people of Gad built up Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
32.36: Beth-Nimrah, and Beth-Haran—fortified cities with enclosures for their sheep.
32.37: The people of Reuben built up Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
32.38: Nebo, Baal-Meon (after changin' its name), and Sibmah. They also renamed the cities they rebuilt.
32.39: The family of Machir, son of Manasseh, went and took Gilead from the Amorites and kicked them out.
32.40: So Moses gave Gilead to the Machir clan of Manasseh, and they settled there.
32.41: Then Jair, son of Manasseh, went out and took over some villages, namin' them Havvoth-Jair.
32.42: And Nobah went and conquered Kenath and its surrounding villages and named it after himself—Nobah.

33.1: These the places the Israelites traveled through when they left Egypt, movin' out in their groups under Moses and Aaron.
33.2: Moses wrote down all their stops, just like the Lord told him. Here's how their journey went, spot by spot.
33.3: They rolled out from Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month, the day after Passover. Israel stepped out bold, right in front of all the Egyptians.
33.4: Meanwhile, the Egyptians was still burying all their firstborn that the Lord had wiped out. Plus, the Lord had put judgment on all their fake gods.
33.5: Israel left Rameses and camped at Succoth.
33.6: Then they rolled out from Succoth and set up camp at Etham, right on the edge of the wilderness.
33.7: They left Etham and turned back toward Pi Hahiroth, near Baal Zephon, and set up camp near Migdol.
33.8: From there, they left Hahiroth and passed through the sea into the wilderness. After three days of travel through the Wilderness of Etham, they stopped at Marah.
33.9: Then they moved from Marah and reached Elim. Elim had twelve water springs and seventy palm trees, so they camped out there.
33.10: They left Elim and set up camp by the Red Sea.
33.11: Then they moved from the Red Sea and camped in the Wilderness of Sin.
33.12: From the Wilderness of Sin, they traveled to Dophkah and set up camp.
33.13: They left Dophkah and camped at Alush.
33.14: From Alush, they moved and camped at Rephidim, where they ain't have no water to drink.
33.15: They left Rephidim and camped in the Wilderness of Sinai.
33.16: From the Wilderness of Sinai, they traveled to Kibroth-Hattaavah and camped there.
33.17: They left Kibroth-Hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
33.18: Then they left Hazeroth and set up camp at Rithmah.
33.19: From Rithmah, they moved and camped at Rimmon Perez.
33.20: Then they left Rimmon Perez and camped at Libnah.
33.21: They moved from Libnah and set up camp at Rissah.
33.22: Then they traveled from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
33.23: They left Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
33.24: From Mount Shepher, they traveled and set up camp at Haradah.
33.25: Then they left Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
33.26: They moved from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
33.27: Then they left Tahath and camped at Terah.
33.28: They rolled out from Terah and camped at Mithkah.
33.29: Then they moved from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
33.30: From Hashmonah, they traveled and set up camp at Moseroth.
33.31: Then they left Moseroth and camped at Bene Jaakan.
33.32: They moved from Bene Jaakan and set up camp at Hor Hagidgad.
33.33: Then they left Hor Hagidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
33.34: From Jotbathah, they traveled and camped at Abronah.
33.35: Then they left Abronah and camped at Ezion Geber.
33.36: They left Ezion Geber and camped in the Wilderness of Zin, at Kadesh.
33.37: Then they moved from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, right on the edge of Edom's land.
33.38: That's where Aaron the priest climbed Mount Hor at the Lord's command and died in the fortieth year after Israel left Egypt, on the first day of the fifth month.
33.39: Aaron was 123 years old when he passed on Mount Hor.
33.40: Around that time, the king of Arad—the Canaanite king in the South of Canaan—heard that Israel was coming.
33.41: From Mount Hor, they traveled and camped at Zalmonah.
33.42: Then they left Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
33.43: From Punon, they moved and camped at Oboth.
33.44: Then they left Oboth and camped at Ije Abarim, on the border of Moab.
33.45: They left Ijim and camped at Dibon Gad.
33.46: From Dibon Gad, they traveled and camped at Almon Diblathaim.
33.47: Then they moved from Almon Diblathaim and camped in the Abarim Mountains, near Nebo.
33.48: They left the Abarim Mountains and camped in the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.
33.49: They set up camp right along the Jordan River, from Beth Jesimoth all the way to the Abel Acacia Grove in the Moab plains.
33.50: Then the Lord spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab, near the Jordan across from Jericho, sayin',
33.51: 'Tell the Israelites: When y'all cross over the Jordan into Canaan,'
33.52: 'You gotta drive out everybody livin' there, tear down all their stone idols, destroy all their metal statues, and knock down their high places of worship.'
33.53: 'Take the land from them and live there, 'cause I'm givin' it to you to own.'
33.54: 'Divide up the land between y'all by family groups. The bigger families get more land, and the smaller ones get less. Each person's inheritance gon' be decided by casting lots.'
33.55: 'But if y'all don't drive out the folks already livin' there, they gon' be a constant problem—like thorns in your eyes and in your side. They gon' cause y'all all kinds of trouble in the land where you settle.'
33.56: 'And if y'all don't handle them, I'ma do to you what I planned to do to them!'

34.2: 'Tell the Israelites: When y'all get into Canaan, this the land y'all gon' inherit—it's already marked out.'
34.3: 'The southern border starts in the Wilderness of Zin, right by Edom. From there, it stretches east to the end of the Salt Sea.'
34.4: 'Then it curves south past the Ascent of Akrabbim, keeps going through Zin, and passes south of Kadesh Barnea. From there, it moves on to Hazar Addar and continues to Azmon.'
34.5: 'From Azmon, the border bends toward the Brook of Egypt and ends at the sea.'
34.6: 'For the western border, y'all got the Great Sea—that's y'all's whole west side.'
34.7: 'Now for the north side: Start from the Great Sea and draw the border up to Mount Hor.'
34.8: 'From Mount Hor, the border stretches out to the entrance of Hamath, then heads toward Zedad.'
34.9: 'After that, it runs to Ziphron and stops at Hazar Enan. That's y'all's northern border.'
34.10: 'Now for the east side: Start from Hazar Enan and mark a line down to Shepham.'
34.11: 'From Shepham, the border drops down to Riblah, which is east of Ain. Then it keeps going down till it reaches the east side of the Sea of Chinnereth.'
34.12: 'From there, the border follows the Jordan River all the way down to the Salt Sea. That's the full outline of y'all's land.'
34.13: Then Moses told the Israelites, 'This the land y'all gon' divide by lot, just like the Lord said. It's for the nine and a half tribes.'
34.14: 'The tribes of Reuben and Gad, plus half the tribe of Manasseh, already got their land.'
34.15: 'They settled on the east side of the Jordan, across from Jericho, where the sun rises.'
34.17: 'These the men that gon' divide the land among y'all: Eleazar the priest and Joshua, son of Nun.'
34.18: 'Also, grab one leader from each tribe to help split the land.'
34.19: 'Here go the names of the ones chosen: From Judah, Caleb, son of Jephunneh.'
34.23: 'From Joseph's sons: For Manasseh, Hanniel, son of Ephod.'
34.29: These the ones the Lord picked to divide the land of Canaan among the Israelites.

35.1: Then the Lord spoke to Moses while they was out in the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho, sayin':
35.2: 'Tell the Israelites to set aside some cities for the Levites from the land they inherit, so the Levites got places to live. Also, give 'em some land around the cities for their livestock and animals.'
35.3: 'These cities gon' be where the Levites stay, and the open land gon' be for their cows, sheep, and all they animals.'
35.4: 'The open land around the cities y'all give 'em should stretch a thousand cubits out from the city walls.'
35.5: 'Then measure two thousand cubits out from the city on the east, south, west, and north sides—the city sittin' in the middle. This the land the Levites get.'
35.6: 'Of these cities, set aside six as places of refuge for folks who accidentally kill somebody. Then, give 'em forty-two more cities.'
35.7: 'So in total, the Levites gon' have forty-eight cities, plus the open land around 'em.'
35.8: 'These cities gotta come from all the Israelites. The bigger tribes give more, the smaller ones give less, but everybody gotta contribute based on what they inherit.'
35.9: Then the Lord spoke to Moses again, sayin',
35.10: 'Tell the Israelites: When y'all cross the Jordan into Canaan,'
35.11: 'Y'all gotta set up cities of refuge where folks can run if they kill somebody on accident.'
35.12: 'These cities gon' be a safe place from anybody tryin' to get revenge, so the person who did it got a chance to stand trial before the people.'
35.13: 'Make sure y'all got six of these refuge cities.'
35.14: 'Put three on the east side of the Jordan and three in Canaan.'
35.15: 'These six cities of refuge gon' be for everybody—the Israelites, the foreigners, and anybody livin' among y'all—so if somebody kills by accident, they got somewhere to run.'
35.16: 'But listen, if somebody kills with an iron tool, that's murder—they guilty and gotta die.'
35.17: 'Same if they hit somebody with a big enough rock to kill 'em, they a murderer—put 'em to death.'
35.18: 'Or if they use a wooden weapon to kill somebody, that's murder—put 'em to death.'
35.19: 'The family member seekin' justice—the avenger of blood—gotta put the murderer down when they catch 'em.'
35.20: 'If they kill somebody outta hate, or they layin' in wait and throw somethin' to kill 'em,'
35.21: 'Or they hit somebody outta spite and the person dies, that's murder—the avenger of blood gotta put 'em to death when they catch 'em.'
35.22: 'But if they push somebody by accident, or throw somethin' without meanin' to hit 'em,'
35.23: 'Or they drop a rock on somebody they ain't see, and it kills 'em, but they ain't got beef with that person,'
35.24: 'Then the community gotta decide if it was an accident or murder, based on these rules.'
35.25: 'If it was an accident, the community gotta send the person back to the city of refuge, where they gotta stay until the high priest who got anointed with holy oil dies.'
35.26: 'If the person leaves the city of refuge at any time,'
35.27: 'And the avenger of blood finds 'em outside and kills 'em, they ain't guilty.'
35.28: 'That person supposed to stay in the city of refuge till the high priest dies. After that, they free to go home.'
35.29: 'These rules apply to y'all from now on, everywhere y'all live.'
35.30: 'If somebody kills another person, they gotta be put to death, but only if two or more witnesses confirm it. One witness ain't enough for the death penalty.'
35.31: 'Don't take no ransom for a murderer—they guilty, they gotta die.'
35.32: 'And don't take no ransom to let somebody leave a city of refuge before the high priest dies.'
35.33: 'Don't let bloodshed pollute the land. Blood makes the land dirty, and only the blood of the one who shed it can make it right again.'
35.34: 'So don't defile the land y'all live in, 'cause I, the Lord, stay there with y'all.'

36.1: The heads of the families from Gilead's clan—the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, from Joseph's tribe—came up to Moses and the Israelite leaders.
36.2: They said, 'The Lord told Moses to divide the land among the Israelites by lot. And the Lord also told Moses to make sure our brother Zelophehad's land went to his daughters.'
36.3: 'But if they marry outside our tribe, their land gon' be added to the tribe they marry into, and we gon' lose some of our family's inheritance.'
36.4: 'And when the Jubilee year comes around, their land gon' officially belong to their husband's tribe, takin' it away from ours for good.'
36.5: So Moses, doin' what the Lord told him, said to the Israelites, 'What y'all sayin' is right.'
36.6: 'Here's what the Lord commands about Zelophehad's daughters: They can marry whoever they want, long as they marry inside their own tribe.'
36.7: 'That way, inheritances stay where they supposed to be, and land don't move from one tribe to another.'
36.8: 'If a woman inherits land from her daddy, she gotta marry within her tribe so that the land stays with her people.'
36.9: 'No inheritance should switch tribes—every tribe gotta keep what's theirs.'
36.10: So the daughters of Zelophehad did exactly what the Lord told Moses.
36.11: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah—all of 'em married their cousins from their daddy's side.
36.12: They married into Manasseh's tribe, so their land stayed in their father's family.
36.13: These the laws and rulings that the Lord gave the Israelites through Moses while they was camped in Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho.
